861.title: A tile is the harness’s, not the node’s
861.content: Skill harness-tiles: A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides. Named by: A harness’s default rendering, Board: open and close content, Board: relocate content to the trashcan . A tile is a function of a harness watching a directory, not of nodes. If a harness declares visualisers, each one gets a tile; a tile defaults to the theme, and a harness can declare one or more visualisations, each with a title. The tile set is not a new registry — it is the visualiser obligation made reachable. A harness declares its visualisers in its <instance>.json visualisers (HarnessVisualiserSchema), and kg:audit reports which directories owe one. A graph that owes a visualiser owes a tile, so the audit needs no second list free to disagree with it.

862.title: Where a tile goes — the declared route, and nothing else
862.content: Each visualiser is ONE declaration in the harness that owns it: . "visualisers": [ { "id": "library", "renderedBy": "library-viewer", "coversKinds": ["library"], "subgraphs": "instance" }, { "id": "todos", "renderedBy": "state-viewer", "covers": ["todos"], "alias": "todos" }, { "id": "fsh-guts", "renderedBy": "staging-graph-viewer", "covers": ["fsh-guts"], "publish": "staging-only", "writer": ["scripts/gen-fsh-guts-viz.ts"] } ] . | id is the URL segment; renderedBy names a Tool node (the implementation may live anywhere); covers names this harness’s own directory ids, coversKinds graph typologies, over every declared directory of them in the checkout. A harness never names another layer’s directory — that would be a lower layer naming a higher one. | The URL is computed, never chosen. visualiserRoute in schemas/kg/visualiser-route.ts is the ONE function every generator and reader uses: <harness>/<id>/ for the full KG, <harness>/<id>/<sub-graph>/ for one sub-graph (subgraphs: "instance" — one per covered layer — or "directory", nested under subgraphUnder[kind] where the visualiser declares one), and an asset path below either. Every page is written to that route under the site’s docs layer, so the file and the URL cannot disagree. A tile opens the sub-graph view when it exists, else the full one. | A page claims nothing. A page carries only rendered-by: <Tool>, as provenance; it carries no renders: or <meta name="renders">. A directory’s coverage.visualiser is filled IN MEMORY by withViewers from the declarations, never from disk. | Collisions are declaration errors. bun run cat check:visualiser-routes refuses two declarations resolving to one route (or one inside another’s subtree), a page drawn by a Tool outside every route that Tool is declared to render, a page under a route that names a different Tool, a visualiser covering a kind its Tool does not renders, and any renders: or coverage.visualiser on disk. | The short URL is an opt-in alias. alias: "todos" makes <base>/todos/ a redirect to <base>/cat-harness/todos/, composed by compose-docs.ts for every page under the route. An alias that names another alias, a harness, or anything the site already carries at its top level is refused by the gate before a build and by the composer during one. A tile always links the canonical route. | publish: "staging-only": compose-docs withholds the route (and its alias) from a canonical deploy. | .

863.title: Instantiated is a different fact from declared
863.content: Only the harnesses instantiated in the folio get tiles, not every dependency. Which layers are instantiated here is answered by the root index.config.json (instances[]), or without an index by each root <name>.config.json. That rule is index-config’s; the tiles only consume it, because the navbar cannot be derived from the declarations alone and a directory listing is not the question a reader is asking. Dependencies keep a group of their own rather than disappearing, so a reader looking for one is not answered with silence. A harness a KG subscription chose is instantiated by the same file, with no local declaration: its declaration is the substrate snapshot kg:subscribe cached at the pin. bun run cat kg:instantiate <subscription> <harness> writes the config and the harness’s state directories (and, under an index, the harness’s instances[] entry), and refuses a harness that was not chosen, not declared at the pin, or whose needs nothing here holds. The tile is drawn from the snapshot (scripts/subscribed-harnesses.ts): it links nowhere, because nothing of it is published here, and a snapshot that cannot be read is a finding on the tile rather than an empty one.

864.title: Which harness / is — the landing is index-config’s rule
864.content: The site’s landing page is one of the instantiated harnesses. It is never the layer the generator happens to live in, and never the repository’s name. Which one it is — site.landing in the root index.config.json (an layer name or "hub"), or the per-config site.landing flag without an index — is index-config’s rule. resolveLandingInstance in schemas/kg/harness-config.ts reads both, and check:landing-instance is the gate. When the landing is the neutral hub, / is the harness listing (harness_details.html, these tiles) and the todo panel — the landing sticky panel, not a second board.

865.title: “Harness” carries TWO senses, and only one of them is this rule
865.content: | sense | what it means | how you tell | . | 1 — instantiated here | this checkout runs it | an entry in the root index.config.json instances[] — or, in a folio with no index, a root <name>.config.json (index-config). Read the file, not a number quoted here | . | 2 — a layer others instantiate | a base a downstream repo stands up | nothing in this checkout. It is a statement about the layer’s role in the stack | . The rules on this page are about sense 1. Sense 2 is correct usage too: a layer can be declared, not instantiated, and declare no visualiser — so it owes no tile — while being exactly what a downstream repository instantiates. No count is given for either sense, because a count in prose is a claim nothing checks; ask the filesystem. Do not write a checker for this. A predicate on the word cannot separate its two senses, so it is an adjudication, not a check (adjudication). When the word is load-bearing, say which sense — “instantiated here” or “a layer downstream repos instantiate”.

866.title: A tile opens the LAYER, not a kind handler’s view of it
866.content: A viewer page is a RENDERING with its own IRI, separate from the asset it shows; see kg-viewer §”The asset and its rendering are two resources with two IRIs”. scripts/mount-instance-docs.ts carries the two routes: . | route | handler | what it is | . | /<kind>/<instance>/ | the kind’s, cat-harness’s | the default rendering any layer declaring that kind gets | . | /<instance>/ | the layer itself | its own themed root | . The tile’s target is the layer’s own themed root when it has one, and a handler’s viewer only when it does not. The viewers stay reachable, listed beneath. A layer has that root when it has its own site directory, read from its own declaration — never by probing the BUILT site, where a layer whose pages are generated at build time has none until its generator runs.

867.title: Order is the declared dependency stack, reversed
867.content: Bottom to top, computed from the declared needs, never written out as names: a name list is a rule true only for the layers somebody remembered. The spine’s head keeps the top and its floor keeps the bottom. A layer whose layer nobody declared is undetermined — placed below the head, alphabetically, carrying a finding that says its place is not derived. Absent is not []: one is nobody having said, the other is a layer asserting it sits on nothing. A broken graph does not blank the navbar. flattenDependencies returns an empty order on a cycle, which is right for a pipeline and wrong for a sidebar, where showing nothing hides every layer over one typo. The problems are reported and the list falls back to alphabetical.

868.title: Two gaps, reported rather than hidden
868.content: Both are the third state, and they are DIFFERENT findings: . | declared and not rendered — a graph the layer declares with no published page. Not linked (a dead link reads as “this site is broken”), and reported. | rendered and not declared — a page published under a kind the layer does not declare. Also not linked, because the declaration decides what a tile may claim to show — and reported, because staying silent would hide a working viewer behind a rule, and the remedy is one line in a declaration. | .

869.title: An inert row SAYS why, and “no viewer” is four answers
869.content: A declared graph with no published viewer appears in the navbar as a row that does not open. Drawing it grey is not saying it: . | A title on a non-focusable element is a label for a pointer and for nothing else — no keyboard path, and not reliably announced. | Dimming alone is state carried by contrast, and can pass the contrast ratio while saying nothing. | . The reason is content: real text in the row. It is in the accessibility tree, survives a stylesheet that does not load, and cannot disagree with a second signal. Do not use aria-disabled — nothing is a control, and marking a <span> disabled announces a widget that does not exist. “No viewer” is four states, told apart by inertNote (harness-tiles.ts): . | state | the row says | is it a gap? | . | declared publish: "staging-only" | staging only | no — withheld on purpose | . | layer declares renderExemption.of: ["visualiser"] | no viewer by design | no | . | a viewer exists off the conventional path | viewer not published | yes, and a different one | . | nothing declares a viewer | no viewer yet | yes | . One wording for all four would label an intended state a gap, which is as wrong as hiding a real gap. Neither navbar picks the words. They render what the generator gave them, which keeps them one navbar rather than two that agree by maintenance. A kind the generator said nothing about renders with no claim about why.

870.title: A tile, or an avatar? WHO DECLARED IT
870.content: A tile is what the HARNESS declares. An avatar is what the FOLIO holds. | the thing | renders as | because | . | a declared visualiser (the harness’s visualisers) — over a directory or sub-graph | tile, functional | the harness declares it; §”A tile is the harness’s” above | . | a set of schema instances — todos | tile, content | the harness declares the set; the instances are the folio’s | . | a note, a document, a materialised asset in the folio’s reproduce directories (library/, uploads/) | avatar | the folio holds it; it is the reader’s, not the harness’s | . A TILE IS ONE OF TWO KINDS, and they bind to different things . |   | functional tile | content tile | . | subject | a directory or sub-graph | a set of schema instances | . | bound to | a SKILL | a SCHEMA | . | resolved when opened | a tool that implements the skill | the instances | . | what empty means | a gap to report — a skill nothing implements is unreachable | a real state — “nothing outstanding” is not “broken” | . A functional tile names the SKILL, never the tool. schemas/tools/tool-types.ts makes tools that satisfy one skill interchangeable, so a tile bound to a tool breaks the moment another tool is chosen. Likewise VisualiserDeclarationSchema takes “one path, or several visualisations”: a sub-graph may be rendered more than one way. Empty is asymmetric. A content tile opening on zero instances is CORRECT and must not be hidden — an empty board and a person with nothing outstanding are opposite facts. A functional tile whose skill has no tool is a gap to report. THEME IS NOT A THIRD KIND. A theme is a palette and its art; a tile takes the avatar’s declared hue. Theme is how either one looks, never an alternative to being a tile. Size does not decide it . A whole materialised knowledge graph (such as cat-bootstrap or cat-harness) on the glass renders as an avatar. So these two tempting rules are wrong: . | “Many behind it → tile, one → avatar” — a materialised graph is many things and is an avatar. | “Opens a viewer over a set → tile” — opening that avatar opens a viewer over a set, and it is still an avatar. | . Declaration ownership decides: a materialised asset is in the reader’s folio however big it is. The same subject can be both. todos is a content tile in the strip and an individual todo is an avatar on the glass: the tile is bound to the SCHEMA and the avatar is one INSTANCE of it. What is checkable here, and what is not . Tile-vs-avatar is not. Nothing classifies a folio item; the rule governs authoring, and the renderer reads the graph an item came from, so a gate would be a declared property whose check cannot answer its own claim. “A functional tile names the skill, never the tool” IS: a declared visualisation naming a tool id where a skill name belongs is decidable against knownSkills() and the Tool graph. No such tile exists yet, so nothing is gated today.

871.title: The navbar icon row is DECLARED, and three states is not two
871.content: navbarIcons on the layer declaration. A closed set — close, todos, beans, processes, kg, fsh-guts, qr, launcher — because a free string lets a layer name an icon nothing draws. Seven is the cap and it is refused, never truncated: silently dropping an eighth entry would overrule the layer’s decision. fsh-guts is a control, like launcher: a button that opens the discarded-items list and carries its live count, not a link. It is also the way back the discard confirmation names, so that dialog says “the fish in the icon row” only when this icon is on the page, and points at Page settings otherwise (board-windows §”Send to fsh-guts asks first”). | declared | means | . | absent | inherit — walk needs, site owner as the floor | . | [] | show none | . | a list | this layer’s own answer | . Absent and [] must not collapse. The guard is !== undefined, never a truthiness test: a truthiness test turns “nobody has said” into “nothing to show”, and makes a layer that has not declared the field indistinguishable from one that wants a bare navbar. The distinction is kept at every layer: resolveNavbarIcons returns undefined for undetermined, harness-tiles.ts omits the field rather than writing [], sync-docs-harness.ts emits null, and the client draws no row and says so once. The walk is needs, not a second traversal. Nearest declaration wins, breadth-first toward the foundation — the direction resolveSkillDirs already composes. A new walk would be a second answer to “what is this layer built on”, free to disagree with the first. Destinations are looked up, never written down. They come from the layer’s own declared visualisations plus siteLinks, so an icon whose graph this layer does not publish gets no href and renders as a non-link. close and launcher carry no href on purpose: they drive controls on the page, and an href would make them look like navigation.

872.title: The theme avatar: the assignment is theme-mediated
872.content: The navbar’s mark is the layer’s theme card art, clipped — not its icon. The chain: . layer → its sticky contribution → the sticky’s theme → the theme’s imageRole → the layer’s images carrying that role → the card layout → its avatarRegion . resolveThemeBackdrop is the join and returns the DeclaredImage, so the crop comes with it. An indirection is not an absence: look through the theme before concluding no assignment exists. Take the card layout, not laptop or mobile. KgImageSchema refuses a non-square avatarRegion in pixels, and only the square crop can satisfy that: equal fractions on a landscape image give a box wider than tall, and the clip scales width and height separately. A card with no declared crop is a finding, not an avatar: the whole composition squeezed into a small frame is unreadable. Report it and fall back to the mark.

873.title: Where a tile lives, and what it must not eat
873.content: Tiles render in the navbar and on the glass: one declaration, per-surface visibility, never two registries. The sticky board carries NO tiles. | Removing a surface loses nothing only if the others still carry it. Every tile this repository declares names navbar and glass, so each stays reachable. A tile that named ONLY a surface that is not mounted would vanish silently — report it, do not re-route it on the author’s behalf. | board stays a legal value in TILE_SURFACES, and nothing mounts it, so existing declarations that name it stay valid (the “every field but ref is optional” rule in schemas/kg/cat-harness.ts). A declaration saying ["board"] alone is valid and renders no tile; the graph-tiles e2e asserts both halves. | . They are collapsible, with the count on the summary so a collapsed list still says how much is behind it — a fixed-height sidebar of tiles must not push the page nav off the top. Theming comes from the avatar’s declared hue: one hue, both schemes derived, so no tile can be legible in one mode and invisible in the other. A per-instance palette would be a second colour vocabulary beside theme.ts.

874.title: On a folio’s own site, a tile describes the FOLIO
874.content: A page’s tiles describe the layer whose site the page is on. A folio’s own Pages site (an IG repository’s folio-site.yml, a document folio’s folio-staging.yml) wears the platform’s chrome, and the platform’s _data/harness.json comes with it: tiles, counts, icon row, rail scopes and title, every path root-relative to the platform’s site. Unscoped, the folio’s badges show the platform’s counts and its links 404. cat-harness-tools/scripts/lib/foreign-site-scope.ts applies the rule to the data, once, for both passes (compose-docs --shell --instance, and rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site): . | the link points at | on a folio’s site it | count | . | the folio’s own root (/<instance>/…) | resolves inside the folio’s baseurl | kept | . | a page the folio’s declaration publishes at its site’s root (/beans/), when the folio IS the checkout’s root (rootOwnPages) | stays root-relative, on the folio’s own site | kept | . | another layer’s state graph (work items, todos, QA, health, uploads …) | is not linked; the icon says why in words | none | . | a platform content, context or derived graph (skills, processes, tools, schemas, docs …) | is re-based, absolute, onto DOCS_SITE_BASE, with its qualifier shown | none | . | a kind nothing classifies | is treated as state | none | . The state row is unlinked rather than shown at zero or re-based. Per schemas/ui/tile-count.ts, absent is a third state, never 0: a folio that declares no beans graph has said nothing about work items. Showing 0 would be a claim, and showing the platform’s number answers the folio’s question with somebody else’s. The icon keeps its place and its accessible name says, for example, *“ declares no beans graph"* (§"An inert row SAYS why"). Ownership is decided by where the link points, never by a kind of the same name. A folio that declares a qa directory does not borrow the platform’s QA tile and its count; borrowing it because the word matched would put the platform’s number back on the folio’s page. A count beside a borrowed link is dropped too: the link is accurate, but the number would still sit on the folio’s page next to the folio’s own. The qualifier is shown instead, so the tile reads as the platform’s. The host’s count projections are not chrome. compose-docs --shell leaves out every assets/**.json that declares a headline tile count, as it does _includes/generated/. A badge whose file 404s renders as ABSENT, with no number. A figure that is not a tile follows the same rule: . | figure | it came from | on a folio’s site it | count | . | the translation sweep badge | _data/translation-qa.json, the platform’s | the shell leaves the file out; the badge stays, inert, reading “QA: not published”, and says why: *“ publishes no translation QA sweep on this site"* | none, and not “not run”, which would be a claim about the folio | . | the navbar’s locale swap | _data/translations.json, the platform’s index of its own pages | the shell leaves the file out; the index reads as null, “could not determine”, and the navbar stays as built | n/a | . | the fsh-guts fish | a button whose count is fetched from this site’s /fsh-guts.json | the button is drawn only when the folio links its OWN fsh-guts; otherwise the fish is the row’s re-based link, named *“the platform’s: declares no fsh-guts graph"*, or an inert icon with the note | none, never ”?”: ? means the read failed | . A folio that publishes its own sweep or fsh-guts document gets its own figure back with no further change: foreignSite.absent (written by scopeHarnessData) only supplies the words for when the site carries nothing. The two _data/ files are named in HOST_DATA_PROJECTIONS, since neither declares what it describes. foreign-site-scope.test.ts fails on a shell that carries a _data/ file nobody has classified as chrome or projection. A folio that IS the root of its own site (for example one whose site is generated rather than a Jekyll tree) needs four more things: . | Its declared pages are its own. Its visualisers under its own site directory publish at the site root, by the same ownsSite || isRepoRoot rule siteDirMount gives its icon (harness-tiles.ts), and the scope keeps them (ForeignScope.ownPages). | The icon row’s own paths and counts resolve on the folio’s site. After scoping, every root-relative href left in the row is the folio’s, and so is the count.json its badge fetches. rail-standalone-pages --foreign-site writes the row’s data-fa-root as the page’s own site root (rowRoot), while its script and style still load from the platform (assetRoot). | Its mark loads from its own site (ownsCheckout). | An image mark can sit on the rail itself. The rail draws the layer’s tone square behind every avatar; a declared image with ground: "none" (KgImageSchema) is drawn with no tone. | . The pinned rail reserves its width. Hover and focus open the bar over the page, as a peek; pinning keeps it open, so .main moves over (docs-ui.css). The gate is foreign-site-scope.test.ts. It runs both foreign-site passes over a folio and asserts (a) no tile carries another layer’s count or links its state graph, (b) no href is left root-relative unless it is the folio’s own path, (c) the platform’s translation sweep and index are not shipped and the rendered head_custom.html hands the badge its words, and (d) the fish fetches no count from a site that has no fsh-guts. The client halves are in translation-badges.e2e.ts and navbar-row.e2e.ts. A check of a page’s chrome has to run on a site that is not the platform’s, because on the platform’s own site the platform’s tiles are right by construction.

875.title: The glass strip — pinned first, and “+N more” counts the rest
875.content: No tile may be silently off-screen: a reader cannot tell a tile scrolled out of view from a tile that does not exist. | The pinned set is DECLARED, never written into a surface. glassStrip on the layer’s declaration lists the pins in order: { "chrome": … } for the glass’s own controls (todos, filter, settings) and { "kind": … } for a graph typology. It is inherited along needs like navbarIcons, so absent inherits and [] pins nothing. sync-docs-harness.ts resolves each kind to ONE tile (resolveGlassStrip): the directory named for the kind, else the first glass tile that holds it. A kind several harnesses publish gets one slot, and the others wait in More, where their qualifiers tell them apart. A pinned kind that no tile holds is reported in glassStrip.unmatched and never skipped silently. | Fit, not scroll. The strip shows as many pins as fit at the current width, in declared order, and refits whenever its box changes. It never scrolls sideways (scrollWidth <= clientWidth is asserted at 1280×800 and 390×844). | The last tile says “+N more”, and N is exact. N counts every tile not on screen: pins with no room at this width, plus everything the reader keeps in More. Shown + N is always the total. The tile is a button named “N more tiles”; it opens More and moves focus into it. Pins that did not fit come first in More, marked as pinned. | The reader may still arrange. A strip the reader has arranged, by dragging or with the Strip and More buttons, overrides the declared default in that browser. The fit and the count apply to their arrangement too. | It starts HIDDEN. With no stored choice, the folio opens with the strip slid away. Only its tab shows, reading “Show tiles (N)”. The tab is the one control both ways (board-windows) and carries aria-expanded. The reader’s choice is remembered in this browser as 1 or 0, and storage that cannot be read counts as no choice: hidden. | . glass-strip-fit.e2e.ts holds the four fit assertions and glass-strip-default-hidden.e2e.ts the default.

876.title: summary and alsoWritten — what a reader sees, kept apart from why it was named
876.content: A harness section on the landing page shows the declaration’s summary, a one-line gloss, and lists alsoWritten, the other spellings of the name. A description made to carry them shows the reader a naming rationale or spellings that render as one line. Authoring notes belong in description or a _comment. The reader-facing line goes in summary, and alternative spellings go in alsoWritten as a list, never inline. A harness’s sticky shows the same text as the landing page. A sticky contribution declares bodyFrom: "summary", and the card’s words are readerText in schemas/content/sticky-contribution.ts: the summary (else the description), then the alsoWritten spellings after “Also written:”. That is the rule docs/_includes/harness_details.html applies, read from the same two declaration fields, so there is no copy of the text to keep in step. bodyFrom: "description" still parses, because the pinned bootstrap/bootstrap.json declares it. bun run cat landing:sticky:check fails when a card built from its declaration does not open with that text. A bodyAppend may follow the reader’s text, and a card with a literal body is not compared.

945.title: Asking a person, in one reusable way
945.content: Skill human-agent-discussion: Ask a person (or a sibling agent) for what no file holds. First determine where you are — the context, the Role you act as and theirs, the Process and task (or that you are idle) — and ask about whichever you cannot determine before anything else. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question. Named by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Human–agent discussion, Initialize a harness . You are the agent that needs something only a person can supply: a choice, a judgement, or a step only they have the rights to perform. Every diagram in bootstrap that needs one calls processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn as a call activity rather than drawing its own asking.

946.title: Before you ask: determine where you are
946.content: The diagram’s first three tasks come before any question, and each is declared as a precondition of the first one (bootstrap.processes:precondition … before="A_GiveContext"): . | determine | what you must be able to say | why it comes first | . | the context (A_DetermineContext) | what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs it (the layer’s <name>.json, the diagram you are in, the Skill its task names); and whether the question has already been decided — earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes the person’s ruling | a settled question asked again reopens a decision and spends the person’s attention twice. Cite what you read, not what you remember | . | the Roles (A_DetermineRoles) | which Role you are acting as — the lane of the task that called this discussion — and which Role the person you ask holds | an Actor performs a task in a Process as a Role; nothing is a Role by nature. Who holds the decision decides whom you may ask: only the Requestor chooses a harness | . | the Process and task (A_DetermineProcess) | the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to — “Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent” — or that you are in none: you are idle, classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to | a reader who does not know which Process you are in assumes the last one’s rules still hold | . Say all three in the message, as the first part of the context. A caller that already determined them hands them in; you check them rather than re-derive them. You are out of process — the Process is undetermined — when you cannot name it, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand is not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. What cannot be determined is asked first . When any of the three cannot be determined, that becomes the first question of this same discussion (A_AskUndeterminedFirst), and the caller’s question waits, counted. Ask about the outermost first — the Process, then the Role, then the context — since the outer answer usually settles the inner. It goes through the same order as every question below, and it allows no default: a Process or a Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave you. Its answer is recorded, the three are determined again, and only then is the caller’s question put. If it is declined or met with silence, record what is still open and stop: a step completed in the wrong Process records an authority that was never given. I am in Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, acting as the Bootstrapping Agent. I cannot tell whether you are the person who wants this repository set up, or relaying for someone: the request came from another agent’s message. If you are, I will ask you which harness next; if not, I will stop and record that the Requestor is unknown, since only the Requestor chooses. Are you the person who wants it set up? (One more question after this one.) .

947.title: The order is the rule
947.content: . | Context. Where you are (the three determinations above), what is being decided, what depends on it, and what you already know, each fact with where it came from. In the message itself: a link is where somebody goes for more, never where the terms are defined. | Options. Every option still open after you narrowed from context, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. An option you could have ruled out yourself wastes the reader’s attention. | Recommendation. The option you would take, marked, and why. | What happens with no answer. Said before the question, so silence has a meaning both sides agreed to before it happened: the default, when the caller allows one, or “the question stays open and the work stops”. | One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. | . The test before you send it: can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, the question is not ready.

948.title: What can come back, and where each ends
948.content: | what came back | what you do | end | . | an answer that settles it | record it, and who gave it (a person or an agent) | Answered — or, when it answered a question about where you are, determine again and put the caller’s question | . | an answer that does not settle it (a kind instead of an option; two options) | follow up once, narrower, naming what is still open | back to the answer | . | a refusal | record what was asked and what is still open | Still open | . | nothing | apply the default only if the caller allows one, and say so; otherwise record what is still open | Default applied or Still open | . A default is the caller’s to allow, never yours. A caller allows one only when the decision is reversible and its own instructions name the default. It is recorded as assumed, with the default named, never as the person’s answer, and the next message tells them it was applied so they can reverse it. Which harness a repository becomes allows none: a wrong answer does not fail, it succeeds at being the wrong thing (confirm-harness).

949.title: The record
949.content: In the form the caller asks for. For bootstrap’s harness question that is a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json (discussion). For a step only the person can perform (complete-initialization), it is the step with the person’s word beside it. A person saying “done” is recorded as their word, and the next check decides whether it holds.

950.title: Symmetric in its participants
950.content: The answering lane is a person or a sibling agent that already holds the answer. The record says which, because the two are evidence of different weight. Neither is refused, and they are not conflated.

958.title: Human Translation Workflow
958.content: Process_HumanTranslation · advisory · 16 step(s) . The human half of translation: a coordinator assigns a locale to a qualified translator, the translator works in their own tool, a subject-matter expert judges accuracy, and only then is the result official. You are in this process when a person is doing the translating. translation-workflow is the machine half — extraction, injection, staleness — and it hands off to this one at exactly the point a judgement is needed. The two are separate because completeness is mechanical and accuracy is not: the coordinator’s gate asks whether enough strings are filled, the reviewer’s asks whether they are right, and no amount of the first substitutes for the second. What makes a translation OFFICIAL is the reviewer’s sign-off, never the file being complete. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

964.title: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
964.content: Process_IgAstCache · advisory · 6 step(s) . How an IG repository’s own site is published, and how the AST it is built from is kept current (skill ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”). THE RULE. An IG site is built from the IG Publisher AST read from the IG repository’s cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>, never from Publisher HTML. The publish refuses an AST that is not valid for the commit it publishes (ig-cache.sh restore then verify). A later commit that changes no IG input (sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini, input/) does not make the AST stale. THE REFRESH. The cache is written by ONE thing: fhir-harness’s reusable workflow .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml, which an IG repository’s Site publish calls as its first job (ast; template templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml). It runs the Publisher through the AST exporter on a GitHub runner (Java, 10 GB heap, tx.fhir.org). It seeds the branch only from a commit on the default branch whose inputs equal the tip’s. A valid AST is a cache, not a release: every page drawn from it carries the provisional mark (ig-ast-delta). i i i i i i

967.doc: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
967.title: Steps
967.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Restore and judge the cached ASTTask_Restore | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-ast-deltaig-build-pipeline | ig-cache.sh restore --ig-root . fetches cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> into output-ast/ (with the Publisher’s txcache/), then ig-cache.sh verify runs ig-ast.ts validity: exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (naming which input), 2 cannot-tell. A restore that finds no branch is a miss, judged as not valid. In an IG repository’s site route this is the first pre step, ig-site:ast (ig-repo-site.ts ast). | . | Build and publish the site from the ASTTask_BuildSite | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-render-jekyllig-build-pipeline | Runs the site route’s steps via stage-local.ts → build-instance-site.ts: ig-site:sidecars (IG API sidecars, if the landing layer has the step), ig-site:compose (artefact index and thin pages from the AST, the IG composed at the root), ig-site:openapi (if the IG holds OpenAPI pages), ig-site:publisher-pages (the AST’s resources as <Type>-<id>.json at the root, the build stamp), and last ig-site:bar (the IG’s slim bar on pages written after publisher-pages). Published at the root from the default branch, as a preview otherwise. When the restore recorded the cache commit, the site reads the AST from that commit by raw URL rather than copying it: the artefact pages draw each full resource there, the IG API sidecars are read from its ig-api/ (fhir-harness#344), and the artefact index from its fhir-artifact-index/index.json, which the site points at with fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json instead of serving (#358). The root <Type>-<id>.json copies are then reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data; #359), and the JSON-LD graph (artifact/*.jsonld) names each root file first and the cache copy as its mirror. The full resources are the cache commit’s and the release’s package.tgz. | . | Review the site’s sizeTask_SizeReview | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-publication | Read the size report the build printed before its push, and fix what it shows, or raise a decision card with the owner when no known fix applies (skill ig-publication §”Size review”). The report is cat-harness-tools site-size.ts (bun run cat site:size), written as site-size.json beside the build, never into the site. It gives the total against the published gh-pages root, the top directories, the size by extension, the biggest files, byte-identical duplicates, source maps, the directories named after another layer of index.lock.json, and the directories the shared-assets host could serve. Growth over the budget (10% or 10 MB) is a warning. The review is advisory and never refuses a publish. | . | Dispatch AST refreshTask_Dispatch | Publication manager (owner, or the agent the owner delegates to) | ig-build-pipeline | Actions → “IG AST refresh (by hand)” → Run workflow on the default branch, inputs ref = the default branch, force = false. Set force = true only to rebuild a cache that is valid but suspected wrong. | . | Build the IG with the AST exporterTask_Export | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | ig-publisher-fork | The runner mounts the layers the IG repository’s index.lock.json pins, then restores and judges the cache itself. When it is not valid (or force is set) it rebuilds with the Publisher fork (Tool ig-ast-export, litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher at the pinned claude/ast-export commit). A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller’s optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit’s input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The AST just built must itself be valid for the commit, or the run fails. | . | Seed the cache branchTask_Seed | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | compiled-artefact-cache | ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push: one commit holding the AST, the Publisher’s expansions and txcache/, the IG API generated over that AST (ig-api/, ig-api-cache.ts) and the artefact index built from that tree (fhir-artifact-index/index.json, ig-index-cache.ts), which the site reads by raw URL; its subject recording the package, counts, Publisher version and source commit. Refused when the candidate is under 90% of the incumbent’s resources or edges (the no-shrink gate). | .

970.doc: Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced?
970.title: Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced?
970.content: Process_IgAstDeltaReview · advisory · 4 step(s) . The review step of an incremental FHIR IG build, as its own subprocess: list and inspect the differences between the incremental IG AST and what a full build would have produced, then accept them or raise a finding. WHERE IT SITS. In ig-incremental-build.bpmn it belongs between Task_Merge and Task_Qa: after the restored and rebuilt records are merged, before the QC gates read the aggregate. That diagram does not call it yet; ig-ast-delta §”Where this sits in a process” states the placement. WHAT IT GUARDS. An incremental build rebuilds only the cone of a change, computed on the BASE edges. If the cone rules miss a coupling, a resource that should have changed does not, and nothing downstream can tell: the merged AST looks exactly like a correct one. So a person reads the delta, and a difference nobody can explain is treated as a missed coupling. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM. A clean review says the delta is explained, not that the IG is correct. The AST stays a cache: every rendered page carries the provisional mark, and a release is still cut from a full build (ig-publisher-reduction P4). i i i i

976.title: ig-ast-delta
976.content: Skill ig-ast-delta: List and view what changed between two IG ASTs, check whether an AST is still valid for the IG’s current inputs, and render the delta as just-the-docs pages that carry the provisional mark. Read before trusting a cached AST, before reviewing an incremental IG build, and before rendering anything from a cache. Named by: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch, Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced? . Skill id: ig-ast-delta · Package: fhir-ig-base · Layer: fhir-harness . An instance of the general compiled-artefact-cache pattern; the shared contract is cat-harness’s compiled-artefact-cache skill. The AST’s cache is declared once, as the cache/1.0.0 node caches/fhir-ast.cache.json: its verify is validity below, and its staleness is computed by caches:viz (see ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”). An IG AST is a per-resource dump of what one IG Publisher build held in memory. It is written by the ast-export library, which is built on top of the Publisher rather than inside it (litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher@claude/ast-export, ast-export/). This skill is the consumer half: listing an AST, checking it, diffing two of them, and rendering the result for a reviewer.

977.title: The one rule: a cache, never an authority
977.content: Every AST manifest says "authority": "cache" and lists what is provisional until a full Publisher run: indices, dependency edges and versions. Anything rendered from an AST, or from a delta between two, shows that mark to the reader, on the page itself (ig-publisher-reduction P3). A mark that exists only in a log or a JSON field does not count.

978.title: Where the files come from
978.content: | file | written by | says | . | manifest.json (ig-ast/v1) | AstExportCli, AstMerger | every resource with its key, the toolchain, the inputs the AST is valid for, and, on an incremental AST, mixed: true and builtAt per resource | . | dependencies.json (ig-ast-dependencies/v1) | same | every edge, resolved to a resource in this IG or null when the target is elsewhere | . | fsh-index.json | SUSHI (copied by AstExportCli) | the authoritative mapping from source .fsh file to output resource filename, with source line ranges. SUSHI writes it to fsh-generated/data/fsh-index.json; the copy lets a later delta map a file that has since been deleted | . | plan.json (ig-ast-plan/v1) | AstPlanCli | what a delta of changed files means: rebuild, load from cache, remove, or a full build and why | . | delta.json (ig-ast-delta/v1) | ig-ast.ts diff (here) | what changed between two ASTs | . The formats are declared once, and published as JSON Schema . The three ig-ast* formats are declared in Zod in fhir-harness/schemas/ig-ast.ts, and readAst validates through it. The JSON Schemas (draft-07) and a JSON-LD context are generated from that declaration and committed beside it: . | ig-ast.schema.json | ig-ast-dependencies.schema.json | ig-ast-plan.schema.json | ig-ast.context.jsonld | . bun run cat ig-ast:schema regenerates them and ig-ast:schema:check is the CI gate. The Java writer and any downstream consumer validate against these files. Every object is open to fields the writer adds first; authority is the literal "cache", and a manifest claiming anything else is refused. A resource’s key is canonical|version, or Type/id when it has no canonical. Two ASTs are compared by key. An incomplete AST is refused: a missing dependencies.json or a missing or unparsable resource file stops the command, because an empty substitute would diff as “no change”.

979.title: Commands
979.content: All of them live in fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts, and each is declared as a Tool: . bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts list <ast> bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts validity <ast> --ig <root> [--toolchain "<ig-publisher X / core Y>"] [--at <rev>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts digest --ig <root> [--at <rev>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts diff <base-ast> <head-ast> [--plan plan.json] [--json delta.json] [--site <dir>] bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts render <delta.json> --site <dir> bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts jsonld <ast> > ast.jsonld . validity: is this AST still the IG I have? . It reuses folio-assistant-core’s compiledValidity, the staleness check the Lean .olean cache uses. The Java side writes inputs in exactly CompiledInputsSchema’s shape: toolchain, sourceRevision, and inputDigest as 64 hex characters. validity recomputes the digest and the revision from the checkout and compares. | valid (exit 0): built from these inputs. | stale-inputs (exit 1): names which input differs. A changed input/ file is inputDigest; a newer Publisher is toolchain. | cannot-tell (exit 2): never a pass. A manifest without usable inputs, or with a digest in the older sha256:<hex> form, lands here. | . The digest is computed in two languages, Java when writing and TypeScript when checking. A golden vector (58871352384745e1d7fd68f7ea918b0e2febbd86cf36a9cb5f0c7ce9d13a82f1) is asserted by both test suites. If you change the algorithm, change it and the vector in both places; a drift makes every AST read as stale, or a stale one read as valid. A later commit that changes no input is the same source. If the recorded sourceRevision is an ancestor of HEAD and the recomputed inputDigest equals the recorded one, the revision counts as unchanged (sameSourceAs), so a README merge does not make the cache stale. A recorded commit the checkout cannot see (a shallow clone, another branch) stays stale. After a build, check the commit, not the work tree: --at <rev>. The Publisher writes under input/ during a build: it renders input/images-source/*.plantuml into input/images/*.svg, overwriting tracked files and adding untracked ones, so a work-tree digest taken after the build is not the commit’s and a freshly built AST fails its own check. validity --at HEAD (and digest --at HEAD) hashes the inputs as committed (inputDigestAt); in a clean checkout this equals the work-tree digest and the exporter’s. ig-ast-refresh.yml instead restores input/ with git before its check. The toolchain cannot be read from a checkout. Without --toolchain it is assumed unchanged, and the result’s current says so. When the Publisher you would run is known, pass it. diff: list what changed . Resources are added, removed, changed or versionChanged. A version move (same canonical, different version) is paired, not reported as a removal plus an addition. Each changed resource carries a differential: JSON paths whose value was added, removed or changed, capped at 200 rows per resource, with the overflow counted rather than dropped. Edges are listed as added or removed. --plan folds the incremental plan’s decision in. The differential is structural, over the dumped JSON, not FHIR-semantic: reordering a repeating element shows as a change at every index, and a narrative regenerated with a new timestamp shows as a change. Read it as “these bytes moved”, and judge meaning yourself. render: view it in the pipeline . --site <dir> writes just-the-docs pages: index.md (the list, grouped by resource type, with counts, the plan, and edge changes) and one page per changed or version-changed resource (path, op, base, head). | Every page opens with the provisional mark. Do not remove it to make a page look finished. | Liquid in values is neutralised, not merely wrapped. FHIR narratives carry Liquid output and tag delimiters (double braces, brace-percent). A raw block around the page is not enough: a value containing the raw block’s own closing tag would end it. So every value gets a word joiner (U+2060) inside each opening and closing delimiter; the text reads the same, and Jekyll parses nothing. This skill names those delimiters in words because its own reference page is rendered inside a raw block by gen-skill-docs; do not write the closing tag literally here. | One page per key, not per Type/id. Page names carry a hash of the key, as the AST’s own files do, so two versions of one resource are two pages. | Table cells escape |, which a key contains (canonical|version). | . Put the pages under the IG’s own just-the-docs site (see ig-render-jekyll) as a child section, so the reviewer keeps the site’s navigation.

980.title: Where this sits in a process
980.content: The review is drawn as its own subprocess, fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn. In fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn it belongs between Task_Merge (restored and rebuilt records merged) and Task_Qa (QC gates on the aggregate), which that diagram does not yet show: it is what the QC reviewer reads to decide whether the incremental result is what a full build would have produced. The steps, in order: . | validity on the base AST. stale-inputs or cannot-tell means no incremental build; run a full one. | AstPlanCli for the delta of changed files. The planner uses two maps: . | Forward (fsh-index.json, from SUSHI): which .fsh file produces which FHIR resource. This is the authoritative answer. | Reverse (fsh-file-users/v1, from fsh-cone --file-users): which files depend on a given file. This is how a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file (which produces no resource itself) reaches the resources it affects. | . | IncrementalBuildCli (or a full build, if the plan says so). | diff base head --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/. | The reviewer reads the rendered delta. A difference they cannot explain is a missed coupling in the cone rules, not a curiosity: file it as a work item and run a full build. | .

981.title: Which rendered pages a source change reaches
981.content: Before any build, fhir-harness/scripts/ig-rendered-impact.ts predicts the rendered files a change to .fsh, .cql or input/pagecontent alters, through fsh-cone and SUSHI’s fsh-index.json, as a rendered-impact/v1 (skill rendered-impact in cat-harness). An AST diff afterwards confirms it: a resource the delta reports changed whose page the prediction did not name is a cone defect. bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-rendered-impact.ts --ig <root> --base origin/main --head HEAD [--ast <output-ast>] --out impact.json .

982.title: Do not
982.content: . | Do not treat a clean validity as a correct AST. It says the AST was built from these inputs, not that the build was right. | Do not diff a merged (mixed: true) AST against a full build and call every difference a bug. Check builtAt first. A resource carried from the base was not rebuilt, and the difference may be the change itself. | Do not render from an AST whose validity you did not check. | Do not re-implement any of this in a CI workflow. CI calls these same scripts and tools, so a CI result and a local result are the same measurement.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml (ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”) does exactly that: ig-cache.sh, ig-ast.ts validity and AstExportCli. | .
