3459.title: Build the review sheet’s Apps Script and a document’s Config tab
3459.content: Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document’s Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio’s review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft’s pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet’s links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document’s URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet’s Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document’s table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. |   |   | . | Tool | review-sheet-sync | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-sheet-sync.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

3492.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. review-comments . 3556.title: Skills it satisfies
3556.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. dublin-core-renderings . Render a catalogue’s Dublin Core records in the two standard forms an outside reader can use: Dublin Core XML, which a harvester reads, and JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Each rendering is published beside the item’s page. Covers which records get one, which XML form is used and why, how every field maps from the record’s own data (never composed), what cannot be expressed and how that is reported, and the gate. Read this before changing the mapping, adding a catalogue layer, or linking a rendering from a page. Source: folio-assistant-core/skills/library/catalogue/dublin-core-renderings.md. The skill declares no I/O contract (schemas/skills/dublin-core-renderings/{input,output}.schema.json).

3587.title: Folio block screenshots
3587.content: Picture each changed figure, diagram, table, equation or simulator block on the published main site and on a staging build, and compare the two pictures pixel by pixel in Chromium’s canvas. A side that cannot be pictured (page or anchor missing) is recorded as missing, never drawn blank. 3603.title: Check a review log and its repository’s issues for changes
3603.content: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet’s Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository’s open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check’s. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell’s old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row’s Issue cell links yet (Title the issue’s title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue’s URL; a closed issue’s row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log’s Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. |   |   | . | Tool | review-log-watch | . | IRI | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch.jsonld | . | part of | https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/folio-assistant-core/folio-assistant-core.jsonld | . | type | https://litlfred.github.io/cat-harness/v0/ns/Tool | . | declared by | folio-assistant-core | . | source | folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts | . | invoked | shell | . | qa | qa-reports | .

3631.title: HCERT library (Rust, native and WebAssembly)
3631.content: The Rust implementation of the HCERT pipeline: Base45, ZLIB, deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256 (RustCrypto p256, rsa, sha2), CWT, the DVCMin payload, the trust store (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2, trust domains), the section 11 verifier, two-phase issuance and Verifiable Health Links (payload, vhlink:/, the ITI-YY5 manifest, JWE dir/A256GCM with aes-gcm, the RFC 9421 signature base). It builds natively; as the WebAssembly component of the hcert world in api/wit (feature component, wit-bindgen; build-component.sh componentises and transpiles it with the pinned jco into an ES module for browsers and Node, whose only import, wasi:random, maps to crypto.getRandomValues); and as an import-free module with a JSON call surface for the live demos (js/hcert.mjs, with a TEST ONLY builder of self-signed DSCs). 3773.title: Tools — smart-trust-tools
3773.content: The Tool nodes smart-trust-tools declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 18Tool nodes 16skills satisfied 18invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

3778.title: Tools
3778.content: As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 229Tool nodes 102skills satisfied 207invoked as a shell command 23reachable over MCP

3784.title: Who declares each specification
3784.content: A user declares the specification it depends on; the record names no user. That is data-modelling step 8 — the dependent holds the pointer — and it is why this list cannot drift from the code: a file that stops declaring stops being listed. Four forms are read: a @conformsTo tag, a conformsTo: front-matter list, an xmlns binding, and a graph typology whose typing module declares the spec (bean u63y). Every declaration names a record on this page. 3 record(s) nothing declares. A version bump would move nothing that says so: . | foaf | w3c-org | w3c-sparql-1.1-query | .

3828.title: Glossary: Schema fields, T–Z
3828.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2525 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 151 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 207 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 524 terms and is 305 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 524 shown . T U V W

3834.title: Glossary: Schema fields, F–L
3834.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2525 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 151 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 207 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 611 terms and is 361 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 611 shown . F G H I J K L

An IG's site is built from its AST cache, which its ig-ast-refresh.yml seeds on the same push. A publish that starts first finds the cache stale and is refused. IndexSiteSchema.publisher candidate, extracted Which site publisher stage-local.ts uses for this checkout when no --publisher is given: folio, or the kind of a publisher a mounted layer declares (ig, an IG layer's site-publisher-ig). Absent: the declared site.build recipe, else the publisher the repository's own workflows call, as before. It exists for a repository that has both, such as a DAK whose instance declares a folio recipe while its site is the IG (smart-trust-demo). Agents had to remember --publisher ig for that repository, and the shared folio-site-publish.yml that runs on every push to main had no way of knowing it (owner, 2026-11-11: "i want that it publishes once merge to main, update QA reports etc."; cat-harness-tools#1879). 3843.title: Glossary: Schema fields, D–E
3843.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2525 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 151 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 207 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 209 terms and is 125 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 209 shown . D E

3847.title: Glossary: Schema fields, S
3847.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2525 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 151 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 207 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 270 terms and is 156 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 270 shown . S

3850.title: Glossary: Schema fields, A–C
3850.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2525 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 151 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 207 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 517 terms and is 309 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 517 shown . A B C

3855.title: Glossary: Schema fields, M–O
3855.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2525 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 151 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 207 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 228 terms and is 137 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2864 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 228 shown . M N O

3965.title: H
3965.content: health system strengthening A guideline whose recommendations address how the health system itself is organised and resourced — service delivery, health workforce, health information systems, access to medical products, financing, and leadership and governance — rather than a particular condition or population intervention. 3966.title: P
3966.content: public health A guideline whose recommendations address the health of populations rather than of an individual patient: prevention, health promotion, immunization and screening programmes, surveillance, and policy or environmental measures. 4061.title: A
4061.content: ArchiMate model from the glossary candidate, extracted Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance's folio-glossary/v1 terms whose focus is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their skosConcept property (never by name) take the term's prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with --prune along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without --write it only reports; --check fails when anything would change. --seed goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under library/ (--from): an authored model is never a source of the glossary. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/archimate-from-glossary/archimate-from-glossary.ts#archimate-from-glossary .

Block edit and feedback links candidate, extracted Each labelled block's links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor on main, and [feedback] opens a new GitHub issue about the block, from the folio's .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml when it has one (prefilling only the fields it declares: block, section, source, page, url) or as a plain issue whose body carries the same facts. The document build draws these on every block; this Tool prints them as JSON for one block or all. Governed by the block-actions skill. BPMN workflow engine candidate, extracted Run a declared BPMN process as an instance: workflow_start opens one for a subject, workflow_next reports what is enabled, workflow_complete records a step or answers a decision (a DMN-computed one from facts) and REFUSES a step that is not enabled. State is committed under the work plan, so which edge was taken is a record, not a memory. Tools of cat-harness-tools · source cat-harness-tools/tools/bpmn-engine/bpmn-engine.ts#bpmn-engine . AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Apply . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_ReturnForCorrection . Review and publish candidate, extracted Core's shared review-and-publish process (Process_FolioReviewPublish): the reviewer reads the rendered folio and approves it, asks for changes, or sends a working draft to the Authoring Committee. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Call_ReviewPublish . Review and record feedback candidate, extracted The reviewer this folio binds. authoring-document relaxes the base SME step precisely because no single lane fits every document. Review the rendered folio, not a description of it, and record the feedback. The outcome is iterate — back to authoring — or approved for the publication path. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Review . Review each slice candidate, extracted review-task.bpmn, once per slice, in parallel lanes by role. What kind of thing changed decides which review the slice descends into; the reviewer takes on that inner lane's role for the call only. Each reviewer gives the slice's blocks a verdict, and comments on the pull request with the block: tag where something needs saying. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Call_ReviewSlices . Review impact assessment candidate, extracted Committee reviews the agent's impact assessment: - Were all downstream effects identified? - Are the indicator changes acceptable? - Does the logic change match the narrative intent? . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Task_ReviewImpact . Review increment (test behaviour) candidate, extracted Inner loop: the BA tests each delivered increment against the acceptance criteria. They do not review code — they test behaviour. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#BA_ReviewIncrement . Review requirements and impact analysis candidate, extracted The BA reviews the formal requirements and the impact analysis the agent produced. When a requirement changes a rendered surface, the BA (or the requester) also reviews the wireframe candidates, web and mobile, shown wherever the requester will look (the conversation, the issue, the pull request, or several) with staging deep links and screenshots, and chooses one before implementation starts. The agent records the choice; it never makes it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#BA_ReviewReqs . Review staged rendering candidate, extracted Author reviews the rendered feature branch at <pages-url>/branches/<branch-slug>/ and compares against the main site. The staging banner shows the commit SHA. The agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) sits beside the URLs, with its counts and status line. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewStaging . Review synthesised needs statement candidate, extracted The BA reviews what the agent synthesised and checks it against what they actually need. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#BA_ReviewNeeds . Review the adoption candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#O_Review . The one judgement inside it is Call_Adjudication, whose stands / withdrawn this call accepts; public-comment, which calls this whole process, reaches it through here. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_CommitteeReview . Review the change set on its staging preview candidate, extracted The content-change review of the author's branch: its PR lists the PC refs it answers, and its staging preview is the after side of every deep link. A change the reviewers send back returns to the author inside that process. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#CallActivity_ChangeSet . Review the draft publication candidate, extracted Content reviewer, QC reviewer and technical officer review the draft as a whole — coherence, phase-gate criteria, breaking vs non-breaking change. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_ReviewDraft . Review the editorial dependencies candidate, extracted uses[] is what a READER must have read to follow the block — never populated from the formal dependency graph. Once every changed block is covered, the committee checks the editorial dependencies of the change as a whole before judging its impact. Reading order is a property of folio content, so the step belongs to the content process, which reaches the harness's review by calling DOWN into review-task. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Task_ReviewUses . Review the existing guidance candidate, extracted The author reads what the document, DAK or IG ALREADY says on this question, before looking outward. A recommendation that contradicts a sibling recommendation in the same artefact is a defect no external evidence will reveal. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_ReviewExisting . Review the findings candidate, extracted THE GATE: the editor sees every finding BEFORE anything reaches the corpus. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviewFindings . Review the impact with stakeholders candidate, extracted The committee reads the old version, the new version and each affected adaptation side by side on the staging preview, and hears the adaptation team's account of what rests on them. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Review . Review the preview and answer candidate, extracted Members read the preview and answer in their Blue columns, or leave them as they are when the change is right. They record the row's Disposition (Blue): Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_AnswerPreview . Review the schema definition node candidate, extracted Does the node declare what KIND of node it is? Does a widened type carry its mirrors? Does a removed field leave a reason behind, so the next author does not re-add it in good faith? And where the node RENDERS to something the site serves — a colour, a glyph, a theme's tokens — does a Tool maintain that artefact, and does the visual fact have only one home? The node decides; the stylesheet reports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewSchema . Review the site's size candidate, extracted Read the size report the build printed before its push, and fix what it shows, or raise a decision card with the owner when no known fix applies (skill ig-publication §"Size review"). The report is cat-harness-tools site-size.ts (bun run cat site:size), written as site-size.json beside the build, never into the site. It gives the total against the published gh-pages root, the top directories, the size by extension, the biggest files, byte-identical duplicates, source maps, the directories named after another layer of index.lock.json, and the directories the shared-assets host could serve. Growth over the budget (10% or 10 MB) is a warning. The review is advisory and never refuses a publish. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_SizeReview . Review the size against its budget candidate, extracted The index flags an app over its sizeBudgetMB; the site size review reads it with the rest of the site. Over budget is a finding for the author, never a silent publish. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Size . Review the staged form and wireframe candidate, extracted At the deep links. A change is requested through ✍ suggest in its Questionnaire mode, or the questionnaire-change issue form, and says which side was edited: the Questionnaire or the wireframe. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Task_ReviewStaged . And the question a covered skill hides: is the COMMAND reachable, or only the skill satisfied? A skill can be served by the neighbours of its mechanism while the mechanism itself is reachable from no node, and check:tools reports it as covered and is right to. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewTool . Review the translation candidate, extracted Coverage, preserved terms and echoes are mechanical. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_ReviewTranslation . Review translation for accuracy candidate, extracted A subject-matter expert reviews the injected translated markdown for: - Clinical/technical accuracy of terminology - Preservation of meaning from the source - Cultural appropriateness for the target locale - Consistency with the domain glossary For WHO content: the SME verifies that normative statements ("SHALL", "SHOULD", "MAY") are translated with the correct force in the target language. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_SMEReview . Review what the substrate offers candidate, extracted Every subgraph, asset class and harness the cached declaration names, each with its current state — referenced, materialised, unknown, stale, or refused by a gate. Shown whole, because a reader who sees only what was chosen cannot tell "not offered" from "not taken". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Review . Revise the adaptations as decided candidate, extracted Each revision is an ordinary content change, reviewed on its staging preview through content change review, on the re-pin's branch or a branch that merges with it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Revise . Revise the proposed change candidate, extracted The editor chose revise: rework the proposed change against the findings the editor reviewed, then send it back through validation as a new proposal. The before/after preview is refreshed with it (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviseEdit . Round trip on the changed strings candidate, extracted The untainted round trip, with the sample restricted to the strings this run translated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Call_TR_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate the target-language .md into the source language and compare the meaning with the original. It catches semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see, and tells the two apart. Tool: the translation_validate MCP tool. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_RoundTripQa . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, "route drift to a human reviewer"), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. The findings include translation:glossary:check's: every glossary term translated against the locale term base, fixed before sign-off, with its glossary section in the KG QA report. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block's <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO's msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means "not yet run", which is never a pass. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA (back-translate) candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Route every climb through platform.ts candidate, extracted Every platform symbol the sub-KG uses is re-exported from <name>/platform.ts, so re-pointing the platform is a one-file edit. A merge from main is where new climbs arrive; reroute them here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seam . Route it, and watch the queue candidate, extracted A file goes to ingestion; a link or a description goes to whatever will resolve it. Acquisition stops here — the moment a file is in the queue, library-ingestion owns it, and keeping that seam sharp is what lets a resource acquired through a channel that does not exist yet reach ingestion unchanged. An arrival may be minutes or days away, so it is watched rather than chased. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Route . Route the answer back, quoted candidate, extracted On answerRoute, with the person's own message attached by id where the host allows, so the sibling can treat it as the person's approval. A paraphrase is never approval. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_RouteBack . Run IG release (draft) by hand for the tag candidate, extracted Actions → "IG release (draft)" → Run workflow, input tag = v<version>. For a tag pushed before the IG carried the caller, or whose run failed. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-release.bpmn#Task_RunRelease . Run placement, file a bean candidate, extracted The offer produces a DECISION, not a node. placement then decides layer, graph and node kind — it is the step that catches a hardcoded path or a literal naming one folio — and the authoring itself becomes a bean, because work here is a bean before it is a file. op="note" and not create, for the reason A_CreateBeans above states: the engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean. The agent mints the authoring bean itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first, and what this step records is a note that the decision was taken. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_RecordKg . Run publication QA gates candidate, extracted Publication-readiness QA across layers — QC reports, IG Publisher QA, proof status, broken links, build warnings. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_PublicationQa . Run QC gates on the aggregate QA candidate, extracted qa.json is the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes; the reviewer reads the cone's rows first. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Qa . Run the deterministic gates candidate, extracted Template currency, catalogue coverage, placeholder, tag and URL preservation, officiality, kg:locale, and the locale's supplements compiling with no SUSHI error and passing their structural checks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Gates . Run the node audits candidate, extracted check:tools, kg:audit and typecheck. Read the kg-qa sidecar rather than the summary: it is written per node so an inherited defect and a new one are distinguishable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_RunNodeAudits . Run the review-log-watch check candidate, extracted Runs Tool review-log-watch with the folio repository, the saved values and the log's state file. The tool reads the repository's open and closed issues (no pull requests, no issue labelled no-sheet) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human), Change Set (human)) with the last check's. A read with no Issue column tracks only change-set issues and appends no rows, reporting them as issue-unlinked. It writes nothing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_RunCheck . Run the rule's mechanical half candidate, extracted Whatever patterns and terminology the rule carries. A judgementOnly rule has no mechanical half by declaration, which is different from nobody having written one yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_MechanicalHalf .

4079.title: S
4079.content: Say it could not be confirmed candidate, extracted No URL, no probe, or a failed request. Reported as "could not check", never as "not yet" and never as "live". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportUnknown . Say what is being decided, and why it matters now candidate, extracted First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. A link is where somebody goes for more; it is never where the terms are defined. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_GiveContext . Say what moved and where it went candidate, extracted Tell the reader what moved and where it went, so the content can be found in the trashcan rather than inferred missing from a card that disappeared. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_ReportMove . Say where it will be candidate, extracted A measured 404. The author is told the address and that the first build has not landed there yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportPending . Scaffold the folio candidate, extracted folio_init writes content/, uploads/, library/, the manifests, the builder shim and AGENTS.md. Skipped when the folio already exists. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_Scaffold . Scaffold the folio (folio_init) candidate, extracted content/, uploads/, library/, the first manifests, <slug>.json and index.config.json (the layer's config inline in its entry; no <slug>.config.json), the builder shim, AGENTS.md with its stubs, .mcp.json, the session-start hook and the beans store. On the overlay path it declares in index.config.json exactly the markers picked at Task_ChooseHarnessed, and none it was not given. Refuses rather than overwrites when a folio is already present. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_Scaffold . Scan open issues for match candidate, extracted Search open issues, then recently closed ones, by title and body keywords for one this request belongs to. Requirements may span several issues; note every relevant one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_ScanIssues . Scan the environment opportunities and threats candidate, extracted The external axis, first, per Weihrich. Work the source's categories of environmental change rather than free-associating: societal, governmental, economic, competitive, supplier and market changes, each item recorded with what it impacts. An opportunity is an external element that gives benefit; a threat is one that could cause trouble. Both are outside the subject and largely beyond its control — that is what puts them on this axis, not whether they feel good or bad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanExternal . Scan the repo for content worth importing candidate, extracted Read-only. Classifies candidates into library/ (external source) and content/ (authored here), and reports what it could not classify as its own bucket rather than forcing every file into one of the two. Its fourth section, markers, lists the content markers it found — sushi-config.yaml, a legacy dak.json, .bpmn processes, a beans store, library/, Lean, folio manifests — each with its paths, whether index.config.json already declares it (declared, not-declared, or unknown), and the snippet that would. bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/scan-repo-content.ts --json, a plain command any agent host can run. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ScanRepo . Scan the subject strengths and weaknesses candidate, extracted The internal axis. Work the source's functional checklist rather than a blank page: marketing, research and development, management information systems, management team, operations, finance, human resources. A strength gives advantage over others in the field; a weakness places the subject at a disadvantage relative to others. Both are attributes OF the subject. The source's warning belongs to this step specifically: listing strengths on paper "is very different from testing the organization and experiencing the strengths at work", so a strength recorded here is a claim, and where evidence for it exists it is cited. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanInternal . Schedule the refresh watcher candidate, extracted Schedule a fresh session that follows translation-refresh on each layer, so a template that moves after today is caught by its check failing, not by a reader. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Watcher . Schema and constraint checks candidate, extracted Block schema, label prefixes, required fields, constraint rules. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_SchemaValidate . Scope the criterion so it stops applying here candidate, extracted One edit to the criterion rather than ten overrules on the blocks it should never have covered. This branch is the one an adjudicator under time pressure converts into a dispensation, and the conversion is a defect: a dispensation lapses when the source moves, so a mis-scoped criterion granted its way past comes back every time anybody touches the block. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_ScopeCriterion . Scope the sample: items, store, permanence candidate, extracted Three answers, recorded before anything is fetched. WHICH ITEMS: named by the source's identifiers, or by a subset strategy its descriptor supports. WHICH STORE: the knowledge graph or other structured store the import is tested against. PERMANENT OR TRIAL: a permanent sample lands in library/ and is refreshed; a trial lands in fsh-guts/ and is not. The purpose materialize-remote asks for (working or archival) is asked there, not here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Scope . Screenshots, web and mobile candidate, extracted cat-harness Tool wireframe-check: 1280×800 and 390×844; renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each a script entry. A rendering missing either viewport does not enter review. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Task_Screens . Search beans for relevance candidate, extracted beans list --json / beans query over titles AND bodies, open and recently completed. A completed bean is evidence of a decision already made. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/related-work.bpmn#A_SearchBeans . Search issues and open PRs candidate, extracted The repository's issues (open and closed) and its open pull requests. An open PR touching the same files is the collision most worth finding early. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/related-work.bpmn#A_SearchIssues . Search the published slice in a browser candidate, extracted Open slices/search.html?slice=<name> on the deployed site, run a phrase search for a known row, open it so its payload is fetched, and look at the result; send the screenshot rather than a description of it. Report the mode the page says it used (OPFS or in memory), never an assumed one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Verify . Search trusted L1 sources candidate, extracted Ingested primary literature under library/: the sections/*.md tree and, where a document was scanned, ocr/page-NNN.txt. NOTE the known blind spot — a document OCR'd but never re-run through pdf-structure.py has only a stub in sections/, so a sections-only search misses it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_L1Sources . Search trusted L2 and L3 content candidate, extracted Already-adjudicated guidance: WHO SMART DAKs at L2 and FHIR Implementation Guides at L3. A recommendation adopted in a published DAK is evidence of a different kind from a primary study -- it is a prior decision, with its own provenance, and must be cited as that rather than laundered into primary evidence. NOT YET SKILL-BACKED: no skill searches adjudicated L2/L3 content for evidence. corpus-grep is a different task (checking that a gap is really open). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_L2L3Content . Secure the agent's permissions candidate, extracted Once the actor is known and the record is open, check that the coding agent acting here holds the permissions this layer's processes need, granted by a person and recorded, and ask for any that are missing. This is where initiating the harness for an actor secures them, rather than the first denied command. A run that finds them current returns without asking anything; the same process is called on demand when an action is denied later in the session. Vendor-neutral: the agent is a Tool, and its config is written through that Tool's adapter. Skill: agent-permissions. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#Call_SecurePermissions . Seed both repositories candidate, extracted Seed main, then bring the content and the tools in as reviewed pull requests with their history, so neither repository's first commit is unreviewable. The seed includes every publisher the declaration promises (sub-kg-lifecycle stage 10): a qa directory with storage needs .github/workflows/publish-qa.yml, the caller of the tools layer's layer-qa-publish.yml, and test/results/ ignored. Without it the declared store is never written, and once the layer stops committing its results no reader finds them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Seed . Seed the cache branch candidate, extracted ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push: one commit holding the AST, the Publisher's expansions and txcache/, the IG API generated over that AST (ig-api/, ig-api-cache.ts) and the artefact index built from that tree (fhir-artifact-index/index.json, ig-index-cache.ts), which the site reads by raw URL; its subject recording the package, counts, Publisher version and source commit. Refused when the candidate is under 90% of the incumbent's resources or edges (the no-shrink gate). BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_Seed . Seed the cache from the green build candidate, extracted Only a green build of main or a release seeds. Seed writes to the -test branch, verifies a restore from a clean clone, then promotes. This is the save of the declared fhir-ast cache (caches/fhir-ast.cache.json), under its save policy: the default branch only. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Seed . Seed the work plan candidate, extracted The plan becomes beans, so a resumed session or a sibling agent can pick it up. The run's own bean was claimed by the Process_BeanOpen call before this step, so this step only notes the seeded plan on it; the beans themselves are written with the agent's own beans create, which no engine op performs. From here on, beans/ is the shared answer to 'what is done, what is next' — for humans and agents alike. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_SeedWorkPlan . Seed the work plan candidate, extracted The plan becomes beans, so a resumed session or a sibling agent can pick it up. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. 4085.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
4085.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 376 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 218 terms and is 184 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 218 shown . 0–9 A B C D

4086.content: 1 · Declare in place (nothing moves) candidate, extracted A <name>.json entry with its graphs[] kinds. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Declare . 2a · Measure — unassigned column FIRST candidate, extracted bun run cat check:partition. Read the unassigned column before the edge count, and quote BOTH numbers rather than only the one that improved. The edge count can rise when the measurement improves (previously unjudged edges are folded in); that is correct. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Measure . 2b · Prune, merge, factor — or the classification is wrong candidate, extracted The only four moves. Move the shared TARGET first and the importers after; check the target's layer before the importer's; a schema moves with its script. The fix is never an exemption, it is the right owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Move . 3 · Isolate — own declaration, namespace, artefact candidate, extracted Only once cross-edges measure zero: give the sub-graph its own declaration, its own namespace and its own published artefact, as bootstrap/ has (its own declaration, bs: namespace and graph document). Nothing moves yet; the sub-graph now stands alone in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Isolate . 4 · Extract — a directory move, not a file-by-file sift candidate, extracted Only once edges are zero and the declaration stands alone: move the sub-graph out as one directory move, not a file-by-file sift. Its nested declaration resolves paths against its own directory, so moving the folder moves the graph. The five-point gate is in migration-plan.md Phase II. 4087.title: A
4087.content: Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept the new state candidate, extracted Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Act on the answer candidate, extracted Never ask the person again for what they answered. A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Act . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. Process_Adjudication may also leave at End_NotAdjudicable — one entry and no other side is a review or a gate, not a disagreement — in which case nothing below runs and there is nothing to record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted The judgement itself, and the one step nothing here can check: if a mechanism could decide it, the process would not have been entered. It declares NO cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on purpose, and that absence is the whole of bean bvuk. This step used to name three — stands, scope, dispensation — and six diagrams called it: review-narrative and voice-review, whose question those three answer, and four whose question they do not. refresh-materialized asks which side wins a local-vs-remote conflict; there is no criterion to scope there and no dispensation to grant, yet the outcome half ran regardless. Since the caller's question decides the permitted answers, the caller declares them: cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on its OWN call activity, with its own gateway acting on them. criterion-adjudication.bpmn is that for the QA-criterion question. What could NOT be fixed by passing the codes as data, which was this bean's first recommendation: the three branches ran three different TASKS, so a caller handed local-wins would have had it pointing at A_ScopeCriterion. The branches had to move, not the enum. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers: stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the flagged passage (human) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate .
