Adjudicate: prose, scope, or exception candidate, extracted The same three outcomes as the base voice axis. The register is wrong for this block (fix the prose); the rule does not apply to this content (scope it on the voice, one edit rather than ten overrules); or the rule applies and this block is an exception (a reviewer entry saying why). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudication candidate, extracted folio-assistant's adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker's entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation: the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers' entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at "entries for one criterion disagree" — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Agent pass on the changed rows candidate, extracted For each changed row, the agent pass of Contributor feedback on a working draft: Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, Ready for merge = Yes its merge, and a Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook), every row with an empty Feedback (agent) and every row whose Blue cells changed gets feedback in the same wake, in the fixed layout: the ask first (Decision needed: with lettered options, one recommended, and where to answer), then Proposed direction: and Next:, only the tags bold. The work stays inside the row's Selected Sections; a row with none gets a question asking which, and any edit outside them is named on an Outside the selected sections: line. PRs are named as repo#n, which the sheet script links, and it adds a Where to review line linking each selected section on the preview. The agent then runs tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts and fixes what it flags: a cell that breaks the layout, or a PR state that GitHub contradicts. The agent records its step on the Agent tab at once, with the real time. Previews follow main: by default (Config PREVIEW_REFRESH automatic) the agent runs tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts on every poll for every open change-set PR, and also when people act on a change set (new Blue feedback, Ready for agent set to Yes, or feedback asking to update the preview); with PREVIEW_REFRESH on-feedback, only then. A branch behind main gets main merged in (a merge commit), pushed and restaged; a conflict a person must settle is asked in the change set's feedback. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_AgentPass . Agent review of the change candidate, extracted A review agent judges what no checker can: accuracy, voice, exposition, whether the change says what the editor meant. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_AgentReview . Agree each change-set's requirements on its issue candidate, extracted A change-set gets its primary GitHub issue the first time somebody engages with it (the Discuss form, a recommendation or decision on one of its comments, a mention, a PR), opened by the folio's public-comment workflow; any number of other issues may discuss it and are linked. People agree the requirements there, and the committee or editor changes the record with cs-add / cs-remove / cs-title / cs-requirements / cs-committee / cs-merge / cs-split / cs-close / cs-new. Making change-sets is people's, in any of three ways, each like opening an issue: a row on the review sheet's Review Change Sets with only a Title (the sheet script gives it the next id), a change-set issue from the folio's change-set issue form, or feedback that says a change-set should be split, merged or moved. For the last two the agent proposes the change-sets and which comments go where, as a Decision needed question, and makes them only once an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. A comment is moved by typing another change-set's id, or new, in Change Set (human). The issue's change-set section is rendered from the record and put back if hand-edited; the nightly reconcile keeps every issue in line. The issue is for requirements; the PR that closes it is for preview, review and approval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_GroupChangeSets . Agree the release date and comment period candidate, extracted The review committee and the editor agree when the public comment release goes out and when comment closes. Skill: public-comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_AgreeReleaseDate . Announce the branch on the issue candidate, extracted On CREATING the feature branch, comment on the issue: the branch name, the process and phase, and the beans claimed. Visibility is the whole point — without it a sibling session or a human cannot tell that work has begun, only that it has finished. Deliberately on this edge and not inside Phase 6. The three loops back into A_Implement (increment rejected, MVP not ready, feedback translated) re-enter implementation on the SAME branch, and re-announcing on each would be noise. Announce once, when the branch is created. Before announcing, run the collision review that starts any new unit of work (coordinate, "Starting new work"): open PRs and in-progress beans checked against the branch's files and subject, scaled to the blast radius, and the result recorded in the bean before the first edit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_AnnounceBranch . Answer the other four gates candidate, extracted Restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, each answered permitted, refused or unknown. They are four answers to one decision, and Gateway_Gates reads them with size through decisions/materialization-gate.dmn. RESTRICTIONS. 'No restrictions known in context' is a STATE, not a green light. GateVerdict is three-valued for this reason alone, and unknown is never rendered as permitted. COPYRIGHT. What the licence permits for THIS bitstream, and separately whether it permits the derivation. LICENSE-CONTENT.md exists in this repository and the ingestion pipeline does not read it. RETENTION. A copy with no expiry cannot be told from an abandoned one — the same argument bean-blocking makes about a block with no expiry. An ARCHIVAL copy is the exception and it is a specification rather than an omission: freshness() reports it permanent, not no-expiry. SOURCE LOSS. Not hypothetical. The one IRIS record this repository holds carries a handle on iris.wpro.who.int, a regional instance merged into the global one. Only an ARCHIVAL copy of the original bytes discharges this; a working copy cannot, because the derived sections are not the publication. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_AnswerGates . Answer, decline, or say nothing candidate, extracted The Requestor's move. Declining is an answer. Saying nothing is not, and is what the recommendation's "if there is no answer" was for. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_Answer . Append removed with the reason candidate, extracted BEFORE the removal, not after: a job that dies mid-step must leave a record of the intent rather than an artefact that vanished with no entry. A reason is REQUIRED — an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity this log exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRemoved . Append rendered candidate, extracted A re-deploy is a rendering, so it gets its own entry rather than overwriting the last. "When was this last built" is then answerable without diffing commits. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRendered . Append restored candidate, extracted A full-replace deploy (docs-site.yml, the only publisher without keep_files) wipes the branch; restore-staging carries the previews AND this log back in. Its own event rather than a second rendered, because "somebody pushed this branch" and "an unrelated merge nearly deleted it" are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRestored . Append retained with the reason candidate, extracted Records that a removal was considered and refused, or that a preview still stands because a signal fired; without the entry that leaves no trace, and nobody can tell why a preview is still up. A reason is REQUIRED — the tool refuses without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_LogRetained . Append retained with the reason candidate, extracted Records that a removal was considered and refused, or that a preview still stands because a signal fired; without the entry that leaves no trace, and nobody can tell why a preview is still up. A reason is REQUIRED — the tool refuses without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRetained . Append rows for new issues; hide closed ones candidate, extracted For each row in the tool's append list (one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet), appends it below the last row of Contributor Feedback: Title is the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): the issue's first paragraph, Issue its URL. The script gives each new row its Change-set id. No other writer adds issue rows. Then each row linking a closed issue (the tool's closedRows, and the rows just appended as closed) is hidden and its text struck through. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_AppendRows . Append WHO disclaimer (if DAK) candidate, extracted For WHO SMART Guidelines content, automatically appends the WHO legal disclaimer: - Translation not created by WHO - English edition is authoritative original - WHO not responsible for translation accuracy Only applies when folio contentType includes WHO/DAK content. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AppendDisclaimer . Apply it to the other side candidate, extracted The side the request edited is the source of the change. An edited Questionnaire is applied as an FSH edit and the wireframe is redrawn to match; an edited wireframe is kept and the Questionnaire re-derived from it. Then back to Task_Read. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Task_Apply . Apply it, and state each option's trade-offs candidate, extracted Follow the selected methodology as written — adopted whole, not blended with another. At least two real options: one option is not a choice, and a straw option is worse than a short list because it makes the analysis look thorough while narrowing it. Never quantify the comparison to make it look measured. Where a method scores and sums, this platform takes the structure and refuses the arithmetic: the weights are invented and a total reads as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/options-analysis.bpmn#A_Apply . Apply the stated default, and say so candidate, extracted Only the default stated in A_Recommend, only where the caller allows one, and recorded as assumed with the default named — never as the person's answer. The next message to the person says it was applied, so they can reverse it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_ApplyDefault . Appraise and grade the body of evidence candidate, extracted Certainty of evidence per the grading system the folio declares. The grade attaches to the BODY of evidence for one PICO question, not to an individual citation -- which is why this step is after the join and not inside the fan-out. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_AppraiseGrade . Approve candidate, extracted The committee approves the change: the judgement, recorded with the evidence it rests on. Approving is not merging: a self-authored change cannot be approved through GitHub's own review (the approver may not be the PR's author), and a merge needs the owner's explicit confirmation whoever approved. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Task_Approve . Approve requirements candidate, extracted Stakeholders approve the requirements and impact analysis on the issue, or send them back for revision. Only their approval moves the work to sign-off; an agent never records an approval on a person's behalf. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#S_ApproveReqs . ARCHIVAL verify fixity — never re-fetch candidate, extracted Re-compute the digest and compare. An archive is NEVER re-fetched — the source is what it exists to survive, so replacing it with today's version discards the state it was keeping. A mismatch means OUR copy rotted, and the remedy is restoration from a backup, not re-download. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Fixity . Archive → greppable contents manifest candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Archive . Archive the release with the review candidate, extracted When comment closes, the release (PDF, PC/<version> site and the channel exports) is archived with the review record, so every comment's citation can still be followed. Run bun run cat pc:release close, which changes only the release's release.json; the frozen copy is never rewritten. Skill: document-publishing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_ArchiveRelease . Ask BA to create or link issue candidate, extracted Ask — never create. Creating an issue without the BA's permission is the thing this step exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_AskCreate . Ask first about what could not be determined candidate, extracted The caller's question waits, and is counted ("one more question after this"). What is put first is the undetermined one: the context you could not establish, the Role you are not sure you hold, or the Process you cannot place this in. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. With more than one undetermined, ask about the outermost first (the Process before the Role before the context), since the outer answer usually settles the inner. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_AskUndeterminedFirst . Ask for a link or a description candidate, extracted Both forms, named together. A person who cannot find the file often knows exactly what it is, and a description in their own words is an acquired resource rather than a consolation prize. Asking for the upload first demands the one thing they may not have, before the cheaper answers have been offered. Say what happens if they do nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Ask . Ask for review with deep links candidate, extracted One deep link per rendered Questionnaire and wireframe, before and after. Where the request goes — the conversation, an issue, the pull request — is a judgement, and more than one may be right: staging-review's deep-link rule, point 5. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Task_AskReview . Ask ONE question candidate, extracted One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Uses whatever channel the caller is in — in bootstrap, the conversation the person is already in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_PutQuestion . Ask the person candidate, extracted A step the agent cannot do or cannot check from here — switching Pages on without a signed-in gh, granting a permission, choosing between two ways of fixing a declaration. Asked through the one reusable discussion, with the exact step written out so it can be followed without opening anything else. A person saying "done" is recorded as their word, not as a check; the next run checks it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_AskPerson . Ask the person candidate, extracted The sibling's ask, unchanged in letters and recommendation, through Process_AskThePerson: the full chat text first, naming the sibling and that the answer will be passed on, then the card. A tap on the sibling's own card or a Blue-column answer in the sheet answers it too; take the first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_Ask . Ask to authorise the extraction candidate, extracted A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. Declining leaves the graph declared, detangled, isolated and split in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-authorise.bpmn#Task_Authorise . Ask to freeze the in-repo copy candidate, extracted The agent reports the files that would move, their size, the new repository and the commit the copy matches, then asks: (1) freeze it in the kept trashcan now, (2) keep in place until the first release, (3) show the file list first. Default if there is no answer: (2), nothing moves. A green fresh clone is the precondition for asking, not the answer. Non-relaxable. The host keeps a FROZEN copy in the kept trashcan, not a refreshed mirror and not a deletion; the live copy is the remote mount or subscription set up at stage 10. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConfirmCutover . Ask whether it should leave now candidate, extracted The owner decides, from what is measured, whether the sub-KG starts staging for separation now. Asked as numbered options with the recommended one first and a stated default: keeping it in place is the default, and is a real outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DecideLeave . Ask whether to separate it candidate, extracted The owner decides from the measured signals, and also decides the address base for its identifiers, where verdicts about it live, and what its tools repository owns. Declining is a real outcome: the graph stays where it is. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Decide . Ask which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates go in as the options; the recommendation may name one; the default is NONE. What A_DetermineWhere established goes in too — the process, the two roles, the context — so the called discussion checks it rather than re-deriving it; and anything it could not establish goes in as undetermined, to be asked first. The Requestor's answer comes back as answered, or the question as still open. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_AskRequestor . Ask who is acting candidate, extracted The one step that needs a person. Asked ONCE and recorded, never re-asked: memory/interaction.json and the record exist so that a preference stated once is not requested again, which is WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_AskWhoIsActing . Assemble the site candidate, extracted Assemble the site from the merged records: the IG template and a Jekyll build over output/. Only site assembly happens here — every artefact record already exists. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Site . Assess downstream impact candidate, extracted Agent reviews downstream implications: - Will indicators need adjustment? - Will referral/follow-up for next visit be impacted? - Are translations affected (re-extract POT)? - Do Lean proofs still hold? skill: integration-watcher, translation-manager . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_AssessImpact . Assign to committee members candidate, extracted public-comment assign: by GitHub login. A committee member who recommends on an unassigned comment is assigned it as they do. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_Assign . Assign to qualified human translator candidate, extracted The coordinator assigns the translation to a qualified translator, ideally a domain SME for the content area. For WHO content, the translator should be familiar with WHO SMART Guidelines terminology. The assignment includes: - The .pot file(s) from extraction - The domain glossary - Context notes (block kind, chapter, content area) - The deadline . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AssignTranslator . Attach the evidence candidate, extracted The PICO, the graded body of evidence, each verified citation and its resolved authority record are written onto the recommendation block, so a reader can retrace the whole chain from the sentence back to the source. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_AttachEvidence . Audit the code nodes the increment adds candidate, extracted Descend into the review task for what this increment CHANGED IN THE GRAPH — Tool definitions in tools/ and schema definition nodes under schemas/. It runs before the summary, and therefore before an MVP can be shared: a Tool or schema node shipped in an MVP is the version stakeholders start building expectations on, and a node that names a skill nobody wrote is cheaper to catch here than after sign-off. Called, not inherited: the agent keeps its implementing role and takes on the code-reviewer lane inside Process_CodeReview for that call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_CodeAudit . Audit the graph candidate, extracted AFTER the change, not before. Every criterion here is a join — role to lane, actor to role, activity to skill — so what an administrative edit breaks is not in the file it edited. The sidecars under test/results/kg-qa/ are committed for the reason a printed verdict is not: without them, "unbound since it was drawn" and "broken by this change" are indistinguishable. Runs kg:audit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_RunKgAudit . Author blocks candidate, extracted Every block edit runs the HCI validation gate — see editing-hci-validation.bpmn. A normative statement is a recommendation block, drafted through normative-statements: one statement per block, a folio-chosen label, and its strength as a code in a declared code list, so a reviewer signs off each one individually. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Task_AuthorBlocks . Author FSH profiles candidate, extracted Write the FSH profiles, value sets and definitions the source model calls for. This is the stage where profiles, slicing and invariants belong — a decision that can only be expressed in FHIR comes here, not back into the source model. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_AuthorFsh . Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted The one step no package may relax. A repository cut changes the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to, and that is a person's decision. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Authorise . Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted Report what moves and ask the administrator. A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Authorise . Authorise the move candidate, extracted Report what would move and how it undoes, and ask the owner to create the repository. Declining leaves it staged, ready to leave. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Authorise . Authorise the release candidate, extracted Publication requires authorisation by the programme manager or designated authority. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_AuthorizeRelease . Available to cite as an L1 source candidate, extracted Every knowledge-graph reference to this source now resolves through library/. Authoring and review consume it from here -- see authoring-a-document.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Citeable .

4088.title: B
4088.content: Back-translate the target text candidate, extracted Render each target string into the source language, from the target text alone, using no tools, and say so in a TOOLS_USED line that is recorded. A string that cannot be rendered is reported as such, not guessed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-round-trip.bpmn#Task_RT_BackTranslate . Basic ingestion (harness) candidate, extracted The harness's document-ingestion.bpmn: accept the upload by a declared route, extract its metadata into the KG, and catalogue the asset in library/ — placed if materialized, recorded as referenced if not. Everything below refines that result for a document. Called, not copied. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Basic . Bind the folder to its bibliography slug candidate, extracted Bind the folder name to the document's bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Bind . Blind review per criterion candidate, extracted Criteria: intent-fit, web usability, mobile usability, accessibility, and alternatives considered. A review at one viewport only is incomplete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#R_Review . Branch, gates, PR and review candidate, extracted Called rather than restated. The mechanics of getting an edit reviewed and merged are not specific to the role graph, and a second description of them is a second thing free to disagree with the first. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process code-change-review (Process_CodeChangeReview, sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#CallActivity_CodeChangeReview . Branding: does it read as this layer? candidate, extracted Marks, palettes and art against the layer's own declaration rather than a remembered style. The question a downstream folio makes sharp: would this layer inherit something it did not choose? . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Branding . Brief the topic before touching anything candidate, extracted What am I doing and why is it worth doing; what do I already know, with each measurement's provenance; how do I plan to do it and WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE APPROACH. A falsifier that never fires is decoration. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Brief . Brief the work candidate, extracted What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_Brief . Brief the work candidate, extracted What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written. Here the work is a separation: what is separating, and why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Brief . Brief the work candidate, extracted What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written. Here the work is a sub-KG: what it is, and why it is staged here rather than in a repository of its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Brief . Browse in place, emit a KgAsset snippet candidate, extracted Clean degradation when no write capability (git-push, github-api, github-connector) is present: inspect the asset in place through the zero-write browse affordance and output the ready-to-paste KgAsset entry (with source: { instance, path, ref } populated) so the author can apply it where they have write access. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_InspectReadOnly . Build and publish the site from the AST candidate, extracted Runs the site route's steps via stage-local.ts → build-instance-site.ts: ig-site:sidecars (IG API sidecars, if the landing layer has the step), ig-site:compose (artefact index and thin pages from the AST, the IG composed at the root), ig-site:openapi (if the IG holds OpenAPI pages), ig-site:publisher-pages (the AST's resources as <Type>-<id>.json at the root, the build stamp), and last ig-site:bar (the IG's slim bar on pages written after publisher-pages). Published at the root from the default branch, as a preview otherwise. When the restore recorded the cache commit, the site reads the AST from that commit by raw URL rather than copying it: the artefact pages draw each full resource there, the IG API sidecars are read from its ig-api/ (fhir-harness#344), and the artefact index from its fhir-artifact-index/index.json, which the site points at with fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json instead of serving (#358). The root <Type>-<id>.json copies are then reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data; #359), and the JSON-LD graph (artifact/*.jsonld) names each root file first and the cache copy as its mirror. The full resources are the cache commit's and the release's package.tgz. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_BuildSite . Build and QA gates candidate, extracted Lean build and proof status, LaTeX compile, FHIR/SUSHI validation, QA axes. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_BuildGates . Build and review the locale term base candidate, extracted Before translating: build the locale term base from the layered glossaries, review it, and translate with it. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme's subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term's translation; a layer only adds. A match in another subject area is a sense check, not a violation. Each layer's glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme's catalogue. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_TermBase . Build each IG's artefact index [ig-index-build] candidate, extracted Tool ig-index-build: bun run cat ig-index:build. Restores each IG's AST from its cache branch and writes fhir-artifact-index/ (index.json, menu.json with the source.of/source.ref that Task_Stage clones from, releases.json, package.tgz). A missing input skips that instance, named. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/tools/ig-docs-site-compose.bpmn#Task_Indexes . Build each slice into _site at deploy candidate, extracted gen-slice-sqlite.ts --out ./_site/assets/slices --payload-out ./_site/payload/sha256 --slice <name>, once per slice, from the tree being published: the file, its manifest, the slice index, and the deploy payloads beside the committed KG payloads. Never into the committed docs/payload/, whose orphan audit admits KG nodes only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Deploy . Build into its own chrome-less route candidate, extracted Tool web-app-build (web-apps:build, run with the other declared visualiser writers): each locale's strings are written to <i18n.out>/<locale>.json from the .po (building is the injection), the app installs from its lockfile and builds, and the build is copied to <locale>/<harness>/apps/<id>/ with every page marked folio-navbar: none and rendered-by: web-app-build; the apps/ index lists every app with its size. No other page embeds an app, so it loads only when a reader opens its route. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Build . Build it locally and measure the file candidate, extracted Run bun run cat slice:sqlite -- --slice <name> --out <scratch> and read the manifest: bytes, the row counts, the payload count and bytes, overBudget, duplicateIds and findings. Record the measurement in the work context with its provenance (the command and the date), beside the size of the source it replaces. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Measure . Build staging site candidate, extracted feature-staging.yml triggers: 1. Regenerate docs (schema, skills, content-backed pages) 2. Render BPMN diagrams 3. Stamp build with commit SHA + timestamp + branch 4. Build Jekyll site with branches/ baseurl 5. Inject yellow staging banner into every HTML page A draft pull request is staged too, from its first push. A build takes about 22 minutes, and GitHub Pages about 3 to 4 more. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_BuildStaging . Build the draft publication candidate, extracted Render the corpus into the draft form of the folio: PDF, HTML site, or FHIR IG. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_BuildDraft . Build the IG with the AST exporter candidate, extracted The runner mounts the layers the IG repository's index.lock.json pins, then restores and judges the cache itself. When it is not valid (or force is set) it rebuilds with the Publisher fork (Tool ig-ast-export, litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher at the pinned claude/ast-export commit). A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller's optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit's input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The AST just built must itself be valid for the commit, or the run fails. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_Export . Build the L1 knowledge graph candidate, extracted See ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_BuildKg . Build the public comment release candidate, extracted Freeze the draft as "Draft for Public Comment Release vX": a PDF with fixed line numbers and a site copy under a permanent PC/<version>/ path (not branches/, never deleted on merge). Every channel cites this release's pages, lines and block ids. Line numbers run continuously through the document. Freeze from a FULL build: dispatch the preview workflow for the branch with build_type: full first, because a preview borrows main's search index and slices; pc:release freeze refuses a preview build. Run bun run cat pc:pdf for the line-numbered PDF and its line map, then bun run cat pc:release freeze for the write-once copy under PC/<version>/. Skill: document-publishing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_BuildPcRelease . Build the tag in full and make the draft release candidate, extracted ig-release.yml (Tool ig-release): ig-ast-refresh.yml with force and release (never incremental), then ig-release.ts assets gathers package.tgz (and package.r4.tgz, package.r4b.tgz), ast-data.zip (the AST, Libraries with their ELM) and SHA256SUMS, and ig-release.ts draft makes or refreshes the GitHub draft for the tag. A tag with a published release is refused. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-release.bpmn#Task_ReleaseBuild .

4089.title: C
4089.content: Categorize and summarize candidate, extracted Each hit gets a category (overlaps: coordinate; affected by; out of scope; unrelated) and a one-line summary with its state. Judgement, not a keyword score: say why each is in its category. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/related-work.bpmn#A_Categorize . Check disk against lock against declaration candidate, extracted mount:remote:check, with no network: the lock's pins are the declaration's, and every locked directory is on disk and hashes to its digest. Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. Never drop the copy into an undeclared scratch directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_CopyAndDeclareAsset . Create feature branch candidate, extracted Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit"). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_CreateBranch . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repository candidate, extracted Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_Cross . Cut over candidate, extracted Retire the parent's copy and measure the cutover until it is complete or cannot be shown complete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Cutover . Cut over candidate, extracted Freeze the in-repo copy in the kept trashcan and measure the cutover until it is complete or cannot be shown complete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Cutover . Cut the subgraph that leaves candidate, extracted Apply the editorial scope mechanically and report what it removed. A selection that reports nothing cannot be told from one that ran over an empty rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Select . Cutover: retire the parent's copy candidate, extracted The one commit worth reverting, made only after the parent consumes the release and every identifier dereferences. It retires the parent's copy, frozen, never refreshed and never rendered, rather than deleting it. Where the copy goes is the sub-kg-lifecycle skill's stage 13; this diagram does not name that store, because the published graph must not. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_Cutover .

4090.title: D
4090.content: Data model Entities + cardinalities candidate, extracted Between requirements and sign-off, and the order is the argument: requirements are statements about things, and the model says what the things ARE. Drafted earlier it is invented from nothing, since the entities come from the phase-2 BPA; drafted later, sign-off approves requirements whose nouns were never pinned — which is how two stakeholders approve one sentence meaning different things. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_DataModel . Decide each adaptation: keep, revise or retire candidate, extracted One recorded decision per affected adaptation, with its reason: keep it as is, revise it to the new version, or retire it because the new version now covers it. A decision to diverge from the new version is recorded as such. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Decide . Decide what may leave the repository candidate, extracted EDITORIAL, and it is stage 1 rather than a filter bolted to the exporter. kg-export produces the WHOLE graph because inspection wants the whole graph; a portal wants what its readers may see. Running the second as the first is how a QA verdict, a bean's blocking note or an unpublished draft reaches a public cache. Decided once, here, rather than at each consumer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_Scope . Decide, weighing the recommendations candidate, extracted public-comment decide, or decide: code on GitHub from a login in config.json editors. accepted, accepted-modified, not-accepted, noted, deferred; a reason for all but accepted. Also reopens a decided comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Declare it in place, with its seam candidate, extracted <name>/<name>.json with name, version, repository (the planned home), livesAt (where it sits today), needs, and only the directories that exist, each declared with its files in one commit. <name>/platform.ts from the first commit, so no climb out of the directory ever needs rerouting. Scaffolded by init-folio --staged <path>, which writes those two files and nothing at the host root; never --instance, which writes a whole repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the model where a tool can read it candidate, extracted A model in prose is a proposal; a model in the declaration is a model. Ship a reader in the same change: a model that is only documentation goes inert. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare the mount: harness, repository, pin candidate, extracted A layer { name, source: { remote: { repository, ref } } } in the downstream's root index.config.json, written through writeDeclaredMounts. A folio with no index still reads remoteMounts on its declaration; both at once is refused. ref is a full 40-character commit. Overrides, if any, are keyed by layer name and then by directory id — never by path. The index itself is the index-config skill's. Decide first whether you want a remote mount at all: reading another graph without holding its code is a SUBSCRIPTION, not a mount. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_DeclareMount . Declare the node materialized candidate, extracted The node's state moves from referenced to materialized, carrying purpose, localPath, gates and (archival) fixity. There is NO default state: a node that has not said is invalid, because 'the author did not say' and 'the author said they could not tell' are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the purpose: working or archival candidate, extracted working or archival, and it is asked FIRST because three of the five gates mean different things under each. An archival copy keeps the original bytes, never expires, requires fixity, and is the only thing that discharges sourceLoss; a working copy keeps derived content and discharges none of that. A process that gated first and asked afterwards would be judging a copy whose obligations it did not yet know. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Purpose . Declare the web-app directory candidate, extracted The layer declares a directory of kind web-app in its <name>.json and puts a web-app.json (web-app/0.1.0) at its root: id, title, description, how it builds, the languages it ships (the site's six UN languages: ar, en, es, fr, ru, zh), the layer directories it reads at build time (contentFrom), a size budget, and for a copied app its licence and source. Its UI strings are one flat catalog in the source language (i18n.catalog). No publish script, no site.build.keep, no harness of its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare, detangle, isolate candidate, extracted The graph-detanglement practice, all of its gates: declared in place, zero wrong-direction edges on every axis, and standing alone with its own declaration, namespace and artefact. A plain task on purpose, not a call to graph-detanglement.bpmn: that process ends in its own authorise-and-extract steps, which here are stages 9-13 of this one, and calling it would run them twice. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Detangle . Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant candidate, extracted The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Refine . Deploy the MVP to staging candidate, extracted An MVP is shared AS A branches/ DEPLOY, not as a description of one. feature-staging.yml publishes the branch under branches/<branch-slug>/ on gh-pages and comments the URL on the PR, so the stakeholder who tests it is looking at the built artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work: holding a rendered change back for assessment makes assessment harder, not safer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_DeployStaging . Deploy the preview site candidate, extracted A preview never seeds the shared cache. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_DeployPreview . Deploy the rendering candidate, extracted publish-site.ts commits the staged tree onto gh-pages as a full replace (run by the instance's Pages workflow on a push to main, or by an agent with its own git credentials); GitHub Pages then builds it from the branch. Rebuild and retry on a rejected push; never rebase the branch. The report names the gh-pages commit SHA. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Deploy . Deploy the site candidate, extracted Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. A release's files are not deployed to the site: a v* tag makes a GitHub draft release carrying them (ig-release.yml; skill ig-binary-artefacts §"Releasing"), which the owner publishes. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Deploy . Deploy to branches/<slug>/ candidate, extracted The stage job copies the built site into gh-pages under branches/<branch-slug>/, then staging-share.ts apply keeps only the files that differ from the live site. The preview's staging-sw.js serves every other file from the live site and puts the staging banner back on it. Other previews and the main site are left as they are. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_DeployStaging . Derive content from the assets candidate, extracted See ingest-derive-content.bpmn. Most of this subprocess is not implemented yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Derive . Derive the metamodel in use candidate, extracted Tool archimate-metamodel (archimate:metamodel --check, on the layer root): the element types the model uses and every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern, each checked against ArchiMate's relationship table. Placeholder elements named after their own type are reported, never fatal: removing them is the author's call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn#A_Metamodel . Describe the desired change candidate, extracted Author describes the content change in natural language. Example: "Update the immunization schedule to add a booster at 18 months." . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the intended change candidate, extracted The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the need (chat, issue, discussion) candidate, extracted The BA describes the capability gap in their own words. They do not need to know it is called CRDM. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#BA_Submit . Design review candidate, extracted cat-harness Process_WireframeDesignReview: as-is use for a form that exists, design use for one being designed. This process does not restate the method. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Call_Review . Detect change scope & impact candidate, extracted Agent analyses the requested change: - Which content blocks are affected? - Are there downstream implications (indicators, referral logic, visit schedules)? - Will deterministic logic (CQL/DMN) need updating? skill: content-graph, integration-watcher . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_DetectScope . Detect feature request (crdm-detect skill) candidate, extracted Recognise the request as a platform capability change rather than content work, from crdm-detect's signals. Never call it "CRDM" to the person. Mid-content-work, ask whether to pause for requirements now or record a work item for later — do not switch on your own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#A_Detect . Detect media type, mint a doc id candidate, extracted Sniff the media type rather than trusting the extension, and mint the doc id from the page-1 arXiv stamp where there is one, else from the filename. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Detect . Detect the interaction modality candidate, extracted Before the first question is asked, establish HOW to ask it: audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for a user with limited hand function, large-type for low vision. A user who finds the questions unusable never reaches the rest of this diagram. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_DetectModality . Detect what moved candidate, extracted translation:status --instance <root> for new, obsolete and fuzzy strings, and the instance's template check. Either failing, or showing anything but zero, is a change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Detect . Determine the context: what is known, and already decided candidate, extracted Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the layer's <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person's attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineContext . Determine the process and task, or that you are idle candidate, extracted Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: "Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent". A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one's rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the Process, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineProcess . Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person's candidate, extracted An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineRoles . Determine where you are: process, roles, context candidate, extracted Before narrowing, say where this is happening, in the words you will use in the question. PROCESS: Initialize a harness, at its first step, inside Determine the harness and repositories — the only place a Bootstrapping Agent can be (FR-2). If you cannot say that (you were started some other way, or a step you believed done is not), you are out of process: do not infer your way back in. ROLES: you act as the Bootstrapping Agent because you were told so; the person you will ask is the Requestor — the one who asked for the harness, and the only one who may choose it. A request relayed by somebody else leaves the Requestor undetermined. CONTEXT: what the request said, and what the checkout holds — a declaration at its root, a harness named in the request. Whatever cannot be determined is handed to the called discussion as undetermined, and asked about first; it is never filled with a default. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineWhere . Determine which CDN, the root URL and the Subgraphs candidate, extracted Every Subgraph id asked for must be one the declaration lists; none means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given. The target's Tool is the one that satisfies: ["render-kg-to-cdn"] for that CDN — gh-pages for GitHub Pages. A caller that already rendered and verified its tree hands the tree over instead of the graph, and the Tool pushes it without rendering again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Task_Resolve . Determine which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates are listed and the Requestor is asked, in discussion, which asks through human-agent-discussion. IN: nothing but the context this agent was handed. OUT: zero or ONE harness, and the locations — a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json. One at most: a list of two is not an answer, and the Bootstrapping Agent may not break the tie itself. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_DetermineHarness . Diff the two ASTs candidate, extracted ig-ast.ts diff <base> <head> --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/: resources added, removed, changed (with an element-level differential) and version-changed; edges added and removed; the plan's decision. Every page opens with the provisional mark and is wrapped in raw so narrative Liquid is not executed. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn#Task_Diff . Discuss it with the person candidate, extracted Bootstrap's human-agent discussion, given the composed question. Its Ask ONE question step is where this harness's delivery rule applies: Post the whole composed question as ordinary chat text BEFORE any card. This is the copy that survives: a card, once answered, shows only the chosen option, and a dismissed card shows nothing. Never "see the card", never a request for a typed reply such as "1y 2n". Then the card: Whatever the host calls its selection tool (AskUserQuestion, request_decision, a button card): the same letters and labels as the chat text, the recommended option marked. No host card tool: say so in the chat and keep each answer to one short choice. Its answer step: One tap on the card, or any answer the person prefers to give. Free text is always available and never required. A dismissal is NOT an answer and never selects the default as a choice; the question stays open in the chat. On an answer: Hand the answer back to the calling step, quoted. If it settles how a kind of thing is decided, it is a rule: write it into the governing skill in the same turn. On no answer: Do what the question said would happen with no answer, and say so. Nothing irreversible proceeds on a default: such a step waits for the person. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#Call_Discuss . Dispatch AST refresh candidate, extracted Actions → "IG AST refresh (by hand)" → Run workflow on the default branch, inputs ref = the default branch, force = false. Set force = true only to rebuild a cache that is valid but suspected wrong. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_Dispatch . Dispatch with adjudicator_sees — never the artefact candidate, extracted UntaintedDispatch on the criterion declares what each party is given; the caller names a subject and a criterion and does not hand-assemble a brief, because the party composing a brief by hand is the producer. untaintedPartitionDefects reports overlap when the checker and the adjudicator can read the same file — one of them is then grading its own input, and the verdict measures nothing while raising no error. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispatch . Distribute to the public candidate, extracted The committee and the editor send the announcement through their channels. Comment is open from here until the agreed close. Skill: public-comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_Distribute . Do it, then check again candidate, extracted Only what the agent, or a tool it has, can do without replacing anything somebody wrote: regenerate a README section, add a missing Pages workflow, switch Pages on with an authenticated gh. Performing is not the same as done: the flow goes back to the check, and only the check says done. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_PerformStep . Draft the block edit candidate, extracted The authoring agent produces a PROPOSED change. Nothing is written to the corpus yet. For a rendered change it also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) here, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so the preview exists when the parallel review starts. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DraftEdit . Draft, review and publish candidate, extracted See draft-to-publication.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#CallActivity_Publication . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_Drain . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Drain . Draw the board of todos and beans candidate, extracted The todo board mounts inside the landing board, so harness cards and todo stickies share one surface. Each card carries an edit link only when the build composed one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Board . Draw the sample candidate, extracted On a first translation: every diagram label, every persona and scenario string, and a seeded random fraction of the rest, with the seed written down so the sample can be drawn again. On a refresh: only the strings that were new or fuzzy. Hand the back-translator the msgstr values alone, keyed by an opaque id. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-round-trip.bpmn#Task_RT_Sample . Drop its positions and sweep orphans candidate, extracted Only after the content has moved: drop its positions from the layout layer and sweep any position whose note is now gone. Sweeping first would make the board authoritative over the folio for one step. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_UpdateLayer . Drop the file in the queue candidate, extracted Through the forge's upload form, a commit, or any other route that lands the file in the declared queue. The agent watches rather than chases: an arrival may be minutes or days away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Upload .

4092.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, E–Q
4092.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 376 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 221 terms and is 188 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 221 shown . E F G H I J K L M N O P Q

4093.title: E
4093.content: Edit deterministic logic (if needed) candidate, extracted If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_EditLogic . Edit it in place — it is your own content candidate, extracted The ordinary path, drawn so the process does not read as though every edit needs a copy. Content in a writable directory is authored content and is edited where it lives; the copy-out is for somebody else's bytes, not for yours. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_EditDirectly . Edit narrative content blocks candidate, extracted Agent modifies the relevant content blocks (.md files, block manifests). Validates each edit against the schema (content_validate). skill: content editing, block builders . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_EditContent . Edit the document as decided, on a feature branch candidate, extracted public-comment edit --branch: the author (human, or an agent in the author role) edits the folio's blocks as the decision says, on a feature branch for one change-set. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Quality check: every comment number in the change set has a disposition; the sheet flags gaps and words that differ from the people's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_AuthorEdits . Edit the document in the row's pull request candidate, extracted One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. 4095.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. It is an override somebody applied to get to green, and nobody can review it afterwards — which is why this step is not relaxable. Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). 4098.title: J
4098.content: Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, stated rather than hidden: ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else never reaches it. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. A clean build, a passing suite and every gate can all miss what only rendering the page and looking finds. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge .

4099.title: K
4099.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the edit, re-pin candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

4100.title: L
4100.content: L1 completeness gate candidate, extracted See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Skill-backed by l1-document-ingestion: its section "What a complete L1 entry holds" names check:l1-complete as the gate and states its three results. The gate contains one adjudication (Task_FlagDrift: real, spurious or source-wrong), and its own Task_Verdict records the answer as a reason against the verdict before returning. So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead. From here refresh-materialized governs it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Library . The copy is NOT read-only: it is the copier's own content, makes no claim about anybody else's bytes, and freezing it too would mean the next person needs a copy of the copy. Land the feature's PRs candidate, extracted Phase 6's "explicit confirmation before merging to main", made a step that can refuse. Once per pull request the feature still has open, after the sign-off is recorded and before the issue is closed: an issue is not closed on a feature that is not on main. merge-to-main.bpmn reads each head's evidence live, establishes that the owner authorised THAT merge (a stakeholder sign-off or the BA's confirmation is acceptance of the feature, not authorisation to merge it, unless the owner's own words say so), records the authorisation, merges, and confirms the base. A PR the owner holds or refuses stays open, and A_Close then waits: the BA's authorisation to close does not cover a feature that did not land. An increment the owner asked to land earlier in Phase 6 went through the same sub-process at that time. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process merge-to-main (Process_MergeToMain, sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). Languages: extracted, rendered, and RTL candidate, extracted Every user-facing string reaches the .pot; every declared locale renders without clipping or overflow; right-to-left is laid out rather than mirrored by accident. New UI is where untranslated strings enter, because nothing was stale — there was nothing there before. The node stays referenced, which means the graph still knows it exists and where, and the refusing gate's basis is recorded so the next caller does not re-litigate it. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph candidate, extracted Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link .
