Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . 4101.title: M
4101.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Make the change candidate, extracted content-change-review-make.bpmn: scope the change, branch, edit content and logic, assess and absorb the downstream impact, and push. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_MakeChange . Make the change, check it and merge it candidate, extracted The second phase, drawn on its own page (public-comment-change.bpmn): an author edits the document as decided on a feature branch, the change set is reviewed on its staging preview, an independent QA gate checks the dispositions against the pull request, and each comment it answers is marked incorporated when it merges. A withdrawal still interrupts the comment while this runs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#CallActivity_MakeChange . Map the affected layers in order candidate, extracted Run the re-pin planner (mount:repin:cone) with the fleet and the changed repository. It lists every site downstream in waves, so a site moves only after the layers it takes from have moved, and marks which sites are ready now. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_MapCone . Map values onto palette roles candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark every copy answered candidate, extracted Chat copies keep their text: the question struck through and "[Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]" added. Cards closed with the chosen option. The sheet's "Decision needed" block replaced by the decision and who made it. Withdrawn or superseded hand-backs marked the same way, with the reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_MarkAnswered . Mark incorporated when the change set merges candidate, extracted public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. Ready for merge is set only once the QA gate has passed for the PR's head commit; set earlier, the agent does not merge until it passes. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary that closes its issue. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_Incorporate . Materialise the part candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per layer, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge and publish candidate, extracted content-change-review-publish.bpmn: merge on the owner's explicit confirmation, then remove the staging preview, rebuild main and watch it. An unmerged change keeps its preview. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Call_Publish . Merge into each locale candidate, extracted Merge each refreshed template into every locale's catalogue: new strings arrive empty, changed ones fuzzy, and obsolete ones are kept as #~ entries, never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_MergeLocales . Merge restored and rebuilt records candidate, extracted Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Merge . Merge the one source PR to main candidate, extracted All the templates in one PR to main, merged before any locale starts, so every translator branches from the same main. Once it has merged, its branch receives nothing more: a later fix to the source is a new PR. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourcePR . Merge the PR candidate, extracted Merge the layer's PR to main, then confirm the template checks pass on main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Merge . The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Merge . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Merge . Mirror it to the feedback channel candidate, extracted Review sheet: the "Decision needed" block in the row's agent column, Agentic status Needs you (the document layer's review-sheet-script skill). Issue or PR: a comment. An extra copy, never instead of the discussion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Mirror . Mount each layer at its declared path candidate, extracted Sparse checkout of the declaration and the chosen directories, copied to the mount path (by default the layer's home path, so relative imports and sibling discovery hold). Never onto tracked bytes; never onto a directory no lock says this mount made; never over edits to a previous mount — those are left untouched and reported. A replay of the lock tries the index's layers cache ref first (refs/cat/layers/<key>, then refs/cat/layers/main): one shallow fetch, every byte verified against the lock, and any layer that does not verify is fetched from its own repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_MountInstances . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the declaring directory's storage (or source) — a branch no declaration names is refused rather than guessed. Mount the remote tree at its pin candidate, extracted A remote source: another repository's tree at a full 40-character commit. bun run cat mount:remote lays it down at the declared path and locks its tree digest; it is never written back, because the bytes are somebody else's at somebody else's pin. Usually reached through a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts), which expands a whole harness and its closure — Process_MountDependency. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountRemotePin . Move harness output about it to the host candidate, extracted QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository's, published to that repository's qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. Move into library/<bib-slug>/ candidate, extracted The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Promote . Move it into its repositories candidate, extracted Create the repositories, drain, seed, consume additively, release, and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Move . 4102.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . Name what will move, and where it lands candidate, extracted Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_AskConfirm . Narrative description per image, localized candidate, extracted Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF (Task_FiguresTables), not only to an uploaded one. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library's image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, "Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Image . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeReview . Note the main-branch watch candidate, extracted Second dispatch point: the change was approved and merged, and the root of the site has been rebuilt from main. A failing main build can look like a green run from inside the repo. note rather than claim: the branch-watch bean already exists, and whether the publish SUCCEEDED is not this step's judgement (the build reports its own exit code). A bean is not closed on someone else's say-so, so the step records what it observed and leaves the verdict to the watcher. 4103.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted Each page is read in the document's languages (--lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article's Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document's references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. The options are DERIVED from the graphs this layer declares in <name>.json, read at the time of asking, so a layer that adds a graph gets it in the offer without anybody editing a skill. Never a list typed from memory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_OfferKg . Open the branch-watch bean candidate, extracted First dispatch point for a CI watcher: the feature branch has changed and a staging build now exists to watch. The watcher is DISPATCHED BY OPENING A BEAN, not by a workflow_dispatch: this is a task/workflow initiation. A bean makes the watch durable past the session that opened it: the container is reclaimed, and what survives is the bean. Starting the watcher and recording that it is running are ONE declared step, so the two cannot disagree about whether anything is watching. It notes the watch on the bean rather than claiming it: only Process_BeanOpen claims a bean. The note is idempotent, so re-entering on a later push does not duplicate it. Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. Not between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision: Flow_21b runs Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis .

4104.content: Package with digests candidate, extracted The serialization alone is not a package. A package is an addressable set — the JSON-LD, the assets it references, and a manifest naming every file with its digest and byte count. The manifest is what makes a REMOVED file detectable, which a per-file signature cannot do on its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Package . Parent consumes, additively candidate, extracted The parent pins the pair (a commit while staging, a version once released) — a code dependency as a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json (remote-mount skill), never a submodule — repoints its imports, and keeps its own copy until it is green with the dependency declared. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process upstream-version-adoption (Process_UpstreamAdoption, sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). The loop is the phase: a needs statement nobody confirmed is an agent's summary, not a requirement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Needs . Post it on the GitHub issue, not in chat, and ask the requester and stakeholders to review it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Synthesise . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_MapWorkflow . Phase 4a: Compare the viable options candidate, extracted Phase 4 often ends with a CHOICE rather than a plan, and this is the step that hands it over. Per option: what it does, its pro, its con, what it changes DOWNSTREAM, and how reversible it is — laid out where the rows can be read against each other, then one recommendation and a stated default. A step of its own rather than a line inside A_DefineReqs, because it has a different output and a different reader: the impact analysis is for the record, the comparison is the thing the BA answers from. Folding it in is how it gets skipped — the analysis feels finished, so the options go over as a list of names. When Call_Wireframe ran, its wireframe candidates are among the options: one row per candidate, with a link to its web and mobile screenshots. Skipped legitimately when the analysis yields ONE viable approach. Do not manufacture alternatives to fill a table. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_CompareOptions . The announcement is on the single edge into delivery, so the three loops back into implementation do not re-announce. The engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean — so what this step records here is a note that the plan now exists. If the session cannot write where it belongs, draft it where it can, say so in the file, and open a bean to move it. Place it in uploads/ by a declared route candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing. WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow's ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the layer that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. WHY A PLAIN bpmn:task AND NOT A userTask. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is "Contributor (human or agent)" because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. A note against the ingestion bean is what makes the queue's growth something another session can see. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Place . Place the asset in library/<slug>/ candidate, extracted The materialized branch. The asset lands in library/<slug>/ with its metadata record, its provenance and its fixity. The folder name IS the citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string. The upload is then RETIRED, not left and not deleted: it moves to fsh-guts/uploads/ beside a sidecar naming where it came from and when, and check:uploads-retired finds one that was not. A refining process that derives content from the bytes does so before that retirement; library-ingestion carries the rule. Prepare domain glossary candidate, extracted Builds the locale term base for the target locale from the layered glossaries, has it reviewed, and hands it to the translator with the POT. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme's subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term's translation; a layer only adds, and may not give a fixed term a second translation. A match in another subject area is a sense check for the reviewer, not a violation. Previous translations of related content are evidence for a term with no fixed form, not a source that overrides one. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme's catalogue (translation-manager, "The locale term base"). Writes: a proposed direction in Feedback (agent) (Green), and the row's feedback basis on the Agent tab, so the script can tell when the feedback has moved on. A question for people goes in Feedback (agent) as a Decision needed block with options and a recommendation, and the row's Agentic status becomes Needs human; a chat card may repeat it, but the sheet is the record. An answered question leaves the feedback: its decision is added to the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab, shown in Disposition (agent), whose decision history is appended to and never removed. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Propose . Propose change-sets, as records with no issue yet candidate, extracted public-comment-changesets seed / propose: the agent groups the comments to be weighed into change-sets, one per change the document may need, each a record under changesets/ with its requirements and members. A PROPOSAL: nothing is decided, no GitHub issue is opened, and a comment may sit in zero, one or several change-sets. The record is the only one; everything shown about a change-set is rendered from it. A comment that arrives later is triaged the same way (Tool review-log-watch, cs-requests.ts triage): the agent suggests an open change-set that shares its sections, or a new one, and the committees (TWG) of that change-set, as its own suggestion only; a person's Change Set (human) or TWG (human) on the review sheet always wins. How a change-set came about does not matter: people adjudicate it. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_ProposeChangeSets . Propose the change candidate, extracted Through whichever write tool the session has. The change is a proposal: it goes into the content change review, which decides whether it is published. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Propose . Prose and the code it describes candidate, extracted Descend into Process_NarrativeCodeReview: judge what the pair checks could not settle (a stale pair, a false or undetermined claim), and send a disagreement with a checker to adjudication. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process narrative-code-review (Process_NarrativeCodeReview, sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeCodeReview . Provision gh-pages candidate, extracted Before Pages is switched on, make sure the gh-pages branch exists — the semantics of A_Provision in bootstrap-tools' render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn, first half. git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, bun run cat-harness/scripts/pages-bootstrap.ts --provision pushes an orphan gh-pages holding a placeholder index.html and .nojekyll (idempotent; never forced; the script creates no remote branch without the flag). Then Settings → Pages → "Deploy from a branch: gh-pages, / (root)" — not "GitHub Actions" when the publish workflow pushes gh-pages. Every publishing path reaches this step: new-repo, overlay and add-folio, and an overlay or new repo that remote-mounts its dependencies. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ProvisionGhPages . Public comment on the release candidate, extracted Each comment that comes back through any channel is ingested and placed, triaged, grouped by theme into change sets, recommended on by the committee and decided by the editor (Process_PublicComment). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#CallActivity_PublicComment . Publish candidate, extracted See draft-to-publication.bpmn for the review and release path this expands into. Release authorisation is not relaxable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Publish . Publish docs on their theme's art candidate, extracted head_custom.html sets the ground behind every page of the harness, under two scrims of the page's own colour, so text and links keep the plain page's contrast. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Publish . Publish extracted statements candidate, extracted The IG draws on library sources; every statement extracted from them is published as pages of the IG and in the shared extraction viewer, each linked to its library entry and section, before the IG Publisher builds the site. The sub-process is core's, the same for every content type: this IG supplies only the page look (its pages' table class) and registers the pages in its own menu. The generated pages are checked for staleness in CI. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Call_PublishStatements . Publish extracted statements candidate, extracted The document draws on library sources; every statement extracted from them is published in the document's own pages and in the shared extraction viewer, each linked to its library entry and section, before the document is rendered. The same sub-process ingestion calls when an entry is promoted: here it catches a source the document took up since, and a statement changed since. How the pages look is this content type's, through its adapter. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn#Call_PublishStatements . Publish the draft release candidate, extracted The owner reads the draft's files and publishes it on GitHub: Task_AuthorizeRelease of draft-to-publication.bpmn. Until then only the repository's writers see it and releases.json leaves it out. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-release.bpmn#Task_Publish . Publish the extracted statements candidate, extracted THE ENTRY IS COMPLETE HERE, so its statements are published here. Every statement the extraction captured from this entry (a recommendation, a requirement, a candidate a person still has to rule on) becomes readable in two places: the folio's working artifact, in the pages its content profile renders, and the shared extraction viewer. Each one links back to the library entry and to the section it came from. WHY IN INGESTION AND NOT LATER. A statement nobody can read beside its source is reviewed from memory, or not at all. Publishing when the entry is promoted means a reviewer can check every extracted statement against its source the moment it exists. The sub-process is the same for every content type. The content type decides only how its pages look, through its adapter. An entry that yields no statements (a referenced source, a dataset) passes through it with nothing to publish, and says so. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_PublishStatements . Publish the IG site candidate, extracted Release authorisation and review follow draft-to-publication.bpmn. The site is published from the AST on the IG's cache branch (ig-ast-cache.bpmn). A release is started by the owner pushing a v* tag of the current version (ig-release.bpmn, which also holds the catch-up when a version was not tagged): the IG's ig-release.yml runs a full AST build, then ig-release.ts makes a GitHub DRAFT release carrying package.tgz (and its R4/R4B variants), ast-data.zip and SHA256SUMS; the owner publishing that draft is Task_AuthorizeRelease (skill ig-binary-artefacts §"Releasing"). The site serves each resource as a reduced <Type>-<id>.json at its root; the full copies are the release's and the AST cache's. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_PublishIg . Publish the version with its change notes candidate, extracted The publisher states what changed, what was added and what was withdrawn, and why, in words a country team can act on. The notes go with the release, so the comparison below starts from the publisher's own account rather than only from a diff. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_ChangeNotes . Publish them in the shared viewer candidate, extracted The same statements, with the same two links, are published in the shared extraction viewer, reachable from the site's sources menu. The viewer is the cross-artifact view: every source and every statement extracted from it, whichever artifact uses them. Both places read ONE collected list, so they cannot disagree about what was extracted or where it came from. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/publish-extracted-statements.bpmn#Task_RenderViewer . Publish to the origin (a cache may front it) candidate, extracted Reach host behaviour through publication.host, never by assuming GitHub Pages' behaviour — Pages CANNOT serve application/ld+json and a local server can. A CDN in front is a layer, not the host: the canonical URL stays the origin's, and the cache is an accelerated route to the same bytes. Uploading and exposing are separable steps on purpose, because collapsing them removes the last moment at which a bad URL layout can still be caught. Wrong-direction edges hide in declarations and data as well as imports: run check:import-direction, check:reference-direction and check:process-bindings. 4105.title: Q
4105.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA gate: check dispositions and PR candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA report and one PR to main candidate, extracted Write each locale's QA report, then open one PR for the layer, based on and targeting main. QC gates candidate, extracted The QC reviewer rules on the aggregate QA against the publication gates. Emitting the QA report is mechanical; ruling on it is the reviewer's decision. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_QcGates . Query data repositories and statistical datasets candidate, extracted Indicator and microdata sources. Distinct from the two above because the unit of evidence is a MEASUREMENT with a population, a period and a method, not a claim in prose. 4107.title: Glossary: BPMN activities
4107.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 376 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). Split by first letter. 706 terms are too many for one page within its budget of 1.0 MB, so they are on 3 pages by the first letter of the label. The ranges are fixed, so a term’s address does not move as terms are added. A label that does not start with a letter is on the first page. | A–D: 218 terms | E–Q: 221 terms | R–Z: 267 terms | .

4109.title: Glossary
4109.content: Every term the instances in this repository define or carry, as W3C SKOS. Terms link to the external concepts they match rather than copying them. 3993 terms: 40 authored in 4 glossaries, one page per instance that owns them, and 3953 extracted from knowledge-graph assets in 19 generated schemes, one page per asset type, plus the sources below. | state | what it means | terms | . | authored | A person wrote or approved the definition. | 40 | . | candidate, extracted | Lifted from a knowledge-graph asset's own title and description, verbatim, and not curated. A person promotes one by authoring it. | 3953 | . | could-not-extract | The source names a term the extractor could not read, and says why. | 0 | .

4110.title: Already somebody else’s concept?
4110.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4276 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4276 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

4111.title: Pages
4111.content: Each term is on exactly one page. Authored terms are on the page of the instance that owns their scheme (owner, 2026-10-15), and extracted candidates are split by asset type (owner, 2026-09-24), so that no page is fetched at the size of all of them. | page | holds | terms | size | . | this page | counts and sources | — | 11 KB | . | bootstrap | authored terms of bootstrap | 22 | 28 KB | . | cat-harness | authored terms of cat-harness | 14 | 19 KB | . | fhir-harness | authored terms of fhir-harness | 0 | 2 KB | . | folio-assistant-core | authored terms of folio-assistant-core | 4 | 10 KB | . | smart-trust-tools | authored terms of smart-trust-tools | 0 | 2 KB | . | Skills | candidates, extracted | 241 | 184 KB | . | Tools | candidates, extracted | 68 | 72 KB | . | BPMN activities | candidates, extracted | 706 | 593 KB | . | DMN decisions | candidates, extracted | 10 | 9 KB | . | Schema fields | candidates, extracted | 2928 | 1.7 MB | . Size: this page is 11 KB before compression, within its budget of 64 KB; each instance’s and each asset type’s page has a budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter on each page runs over that page, and its A–Z bar jumps within it. The SKOS files in the sources are the machine-readable form.

4214.title: Glosario
4214.content: 28 / 40 términos redactados traducidos por completo. Estas traducciones no son oficiales: las redactó un agente y ninguna persona las ha aprobado todavía (issue #206). El texto marcado como sin traducir es el original, que se muestra en lugar de ocultarse.

4215.title: Already somebody else’s concept? (sin traducir)
4215.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. (sin traducir) . The table’s labels are in the source language: it reports counts per scheme, computed by the gate rather than authored here. (sin traducir) . Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4276 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4276 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

4216.title: Páginas
4216.content: Los candidatos extraídos no se traducen: se toman literalmente de los recursos del grafo de conocimiento y no están revisados. Sus páginas están en el idioma de origen. El glosario en el idioma de origen, con todos los términos extraídos.

A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync. | . | Bind the folder to its bibliography slugTask_Bind | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Bind the folder name to the document’s bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. | . | Read glossary into candidate termsTask_Glossary | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | glossary-terms | The source’s glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written. | . | Extract reference listsTask_References | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Each reference list of the source (a References, Bibliography or Further reading section, in any of the six UN languages) becomes folio-reference/v1 nodes with the Tool references-extract: one node per cited work, provenance extracted, derivedFrom the section it was read from, and printed the entry exactly as the source prints it. Only fields read without guessing are set (address, DOI, ISBN, year, access date); a cited IRIS item the library holds gets heldAt. A source with no reference list skips this step with nothing written. | . | Link L1 nodes into the corpus graphTask_Link | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact – paper, L2, L3 – resolves to it through library/. | .

4255.doc: Ingestion subprocess — derive content from the assets
4255.title: Steps
4255.content: Every one of the 8 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Archive → greppable contents manifestTask_Archive | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data. | . | File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetypeTask_TechMeta | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable. | . | Narrative description per image, localizedTask_Image | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF (Task_FiguresTables), not only to an uploaded one. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library’s image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Transcribe and translate audioTask_Audio | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | No Tool yet; the method, and the choice of recogniser, is skill audio-transcription. | . | Sheet names, headers, shape, narrativeTask_Tabular | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Tools tabular-csv and tabular-xlsx, as CSVW (skill tabular-metadata). CSV and spreadsheet: tabs, column and row headers, sizes, and what the dataset is about. | . | Extract figures and tablesTask_FiguresTables | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The pdf-images.py, pdf-vector-labels.py and pdf-vector-figures.py arms extract the raster images and the figures drawn as vectors (grouped and rendered). For every table the document’s structure declares, an agent reads the rendered page, checks cell text against the text layer, and writes tables/<label>.csv plus tables.csvw.json (folio-tabular-csvw/v1), with a draft description in the six UN languages; pdf-tables.py’s grid is a cross-check, not the answer. Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris): “actually extract the figures” and “any tables too”. Method: skill document-intake, “Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe”. | . | Footnotes and the marks that call themTask_Footnotes | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | The pdf-footnotes.py arm (owner, 2026-11-11, “also foot notes/marks”): from the page layout, each note at the foot of a page and every superscript mark in the text that calls it, written to footnotes.json (folio-document-footnotes/v1) with the block that holds the page. The section text is not changed. Only a called note is a footnote; uncalled foot-of-page lines and marks with no note are listed, never dropped. OCR’d pages have no fonts and are reported unread. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “Footnotes and their marks”. | . | Cite the author of every narrativeTask_Provenance | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | A generated description is a claim by someone. Record whether a human or an agent wrote it, and for an agent the model version. An uncited narrative is indistinguishable from a transcription of the source. | .

4257.content: Process_ExtractStructure · advisory · 6 step(s) . Extract the structure of an uploaded source: its text layer, OCR where it has none or where a page’s text layer fails the page check, sections, structure and claim candidates. Every step is an arm or rung of bun run cat ingest (cat-harness-tools scripts/ingest-document.ts). i i i i i i

4259.title: Lanes — who acts
4259.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Two provenance paths converge on the same Task_Sections output — an embedded text layer extracted directly, or OCR that leaves the fuller text in ocr/ with only a stub in sections/ — and which branch this lane took is invisible downstream except to a grep that knows to check the fourth tier. Task_Candidates stays a proposal: nothing downstream may treat it as an adjudicated verdict. | .

4260.title: Steps
4260.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract the text layerTask_ExtractText | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. | . | Check each page; OCR pages that failTask_PageCheck | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | l1-document-ingestion | Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris, card Q-ODD-1 = A): “force OCR when a page’s text layer fails a quality check”. A text layer can hold plenty of letters and still not be the page’s text: accents mapped to Greek letters (“dΘclaration”), Persian set in the wrong Arabic code points, words split by kerning (“au g m ente”), fake-bold words printed twice, mojibake. cat-harness-tools scripts/_text_quality.py checks every page against the document’s languages (dc.language.iso, or –lang-hint); the router then OCRs the document and pdf-structure.py –ocr takes the OCR text for the failing pages only, listing them in structure.json source.ocr_pages with the reason. When most pages of a document with no outline fail, the whole document is read from OCR, as for a scan. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “A text layer that is not text”. | . | OCR to ocr/page-*.txtTask_Ocr | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Each page is read in the document’s languages (–lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article’s Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document’s references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently (“Manual” and “Manval”), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. | . | Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matterTask_Sections | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief. An outline is set aside when its entries are machine bookmark names (_GoBack, _Hlk…, “Blank Page”, a merged file’s name) or when under half of them name a heading the pages print, and the contents are inferred instead (diagnostics.outline_rejected). A section that would hold more than half of a document of 20 pages or more (and over 8,000 words), or over 20,000 words anywhere, is cut at the headings inferred inside it, else one section per page (diagnostics.oversized_split). Owner, 2026-11-11: “split single blocks that hold a whole book”. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, “An outline that is not contents, and a section too long to be a block”. | . | Write structure.jsonTask_Structure | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR’d text, source.runContext cites the OCR step’s run context by sha256. A title already known for the document (the catalogue’s dc.title, or one given with –title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections’ doc_title does not carry a scan’s misreading. | . | Extract claim candidatesTask_Candidates | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only – never adjudicated verdicts. | .

4265.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Runs both QA checks unattended and hands off exactly where the role’s persona says it must: Gateway_Drift’s ‘drift’ branch leaves this lane the moment a passage needs a judgement about which of two readings is right, rather than guessing; Task_Verdict, which records the outcome either way, stays in this lane, which owns the completeness verdict as a whole. | . | Reviewer (SME or editor) | reviewer | The only human involvement in this subprocess: a flagged passage where round-trip translation produced two different readings, and somebody has to say which is right. | .

4266.doc: Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate
4266.title: Steps
4266.content: Every one of the 4 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Is every derived artefact present?Task_CheckDerived | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | L1 source to L1 KG is NOT complete while a required derived artefact is missing. This is the gate that makes the derivation steps obligatory rather than aspirational. | . | Round-trip translation QATask_RoundTrip | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | translation-manageruntainted-verification | Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block’s <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO’s msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means “not yet run”, which is never a pass. | . | Adjudicate the flagged passageTask_FlagDrift | Reviewer (SME or editor) | calls Adjudicationdocument-intakeadjudication | A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. | . | Record the L1 completeness verdictTask_Verdict | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Record the completeness verdict in three states — met, unmet, or not yet derivable — as bun run cat check:l1-complete reports it. Not-yet-derivable is never a pass. An unmet verdict opens a bean and returns to derivation; only a met one lets the entry into library/. | .

4267.doc: Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate
4267.title: Decisions
4267.content: Every one of the 2 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Drift or bad terminology?Gateway_Drift | Answered by the round-trip translation QA: did it flag semantic drift or a terminology miss? drift sends the passage to a person to adjudicate, since which reading is right is a human call; clean records the verdict directly. | drift → Adjudicate the flagged passageclean → Record the L1 completeness verdict | . | Which reading was right?GW_DriftOutcome | All three converge on Task_Verdict, and that is deliberate rather than the codes being decoration: this lane adjudicates ONE passage while Lane_0 still owns the completeness verdict as a whole, so the outcome of a passage is a REASON recorded against that verdict, never a different next step. The same shape criterion-adjudication uses, where three outcomes converge on one write because what makes an outcome legitimate is that its reason was recorded.What differs is what gets written and what it obliges. real is drift to fix in the translation. spurious is a false positive, and recording it is what stops the same passage being re-flagged every run. source-wrong points at the SOURCE rather than the translation — the one answer that sends work out of this process entirely, because no amount of re-translating a wrong source produces a right target. | the drift is real → Record the L1 completeness verdictfalse positive → Record the L1 completeness verdictthe SOURCE is wrong → Record the L1 completeness verdict | .

4271.title: Lanes — who acts
4271.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Every step in this diagram is this lane’s, and each treats the source as evidence to be recorded rather than resolved: contradictions in the source are kept as data rather than silently picked, values the source is silent on are marked as a choice rather than dressed up as a measurement, and a missing layout ends in refusal rather than a theme quietly degraded to the ones that were supplied. | .

4272.title: Steps
4272.content: Every one of the 5 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Read the served stylesheet’s declarationsTask_ReadStylesheet | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | theme-art-intake | Read the ROLE, never the prettiest value. Bootstrap’s –blue is a scale entry and –primary is the role; DSpace sets them differently, and taking the brand-looking one is the hardcoding schemas/ui/theme.ts exists to end. Column widths come from declared columns, never from breakpoints: a breakpoint is a viewport. | . | Read the guide’s own stated rulesTask_ReadGuide | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | theme-art-intake | From the INGESTED document’s sections, not from a screenshot and not inferred from a site that happens to use the brand. Units stay as the source gives them: rewriting 29.7cm as millimetres is a conversion nobody asked for and a chance to be wrong. | . | Map values onto palette rolesTask_MapRoles | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | theme-art-intake | surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of “accent colour”, free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. | . | Record contradictions IN the sourceTask_Contradictions | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | theme-art-intake | A step because sources do contradict themselves (one colour given two values on different pages). A contradiction silently resolved is indistinguishable from one nobody noticed, so it is kept as data and the reading taken is stated as a choice. | . | Theme and UI reviewTask_Review | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | calls Theme and UI review — at ingestiontheme-ui-review | THEME REVIEW HAPPENS HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE: graphical assets are reviewed at ingestion, in the context of the website or app design they are for.So this step CALLS theme-ui-review.bpmn.WHAT THE CALL COSTS, stated rather than hidden. The subprocess has a human step, R_Judge: a person looks at the ingested assets laid out in their design at a web and a mobile width. So ingesting a THEME SOURCE is attended at that step. Ingesting anything else stays unattended: it never reaches this subprocess.THE AUTOMATED CHECK IS INSIDE THE CALL. “A theme sets the stripe’s hue; it never sets its width to zero” — colour alone carrying a whole signal fails WCAG SC 1.4.1, and the WHO guide agrees (“Never red with green, never blue with yellow”). That check is A_Accessibility in the called process, which measures contrast against the real ground and requires a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning. | .

4275.title: Every initialization step, as the declarations name them
4275.content: Skill initialization-steps: Walk every initialization step the declarations name (the layer’s own and each one it needs), check each before doing anything, do what can be done, ask for what only a person can do, and report every step as done, not done, could not determine, or stated. Named by: Complete initialization, Determine the harness and repositories, Initialize a harness . You are making sure a harness’s initialization is complete: right after installing it (initialize-harness calls complete-initialization), or because you were dispatched to do exactly this with nothing but the diagram and the repository. Either way the steps are the same, and they are not listed in this file. They are named by the declarations.

4276.title: Where the steps come from
4276.content: Read <name>.json at the root, then each name in its needs, from a sibling checkout at ../<name>/<name>.json. Each step below names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. | step | named by | done when | . | declaration | the file itself | <name>.json parses and its name is its file name | . | needs:<name> | needs | the dependency is beside it, and its declaration parses | . | instructions:<name> | FR-4 | stated: <name>/docs/bootstrap/initialization.md was read and followed | . | schemas:staged | each $id / @id under iriBase (FR-11) | the site build stages every JSON Schema and JSON-LD document at its IRI | . | schemas:published | the same IRIs (FR-11) | every one of those IRIs answers | . | directory:<id> | directories[] | the declared path exists | . | asset:<id> | assets[] | the declared file exists | . | readme | FR-8 | the root has a README.md | . | readme-sections | the README’s own markers | every section the README opts into is current | . | site:workflow | repository | a workflow commits the rendered site onto gh-pages | . | site:branch | repository | a gh-pages branch exists — it must, before Pages can be switched on | . | site:enabled | repository | Pages is on, serving gh-pages | . | site:live | iriBase, else the Pages address | the address answers | . The two schemas: steps are the primary ones. They are checked first once the declarations are read, and the report leads with them: publish-documents. A harness above bootstrap names more steps the same way. A work-plan store it declares as a directory is a directory: step, and a harness’s own set-up instructions are its instructions: step. Bootstrap does not need to know which harness declares what. The site steps are in publish-site.

4277.title: Four states, not two
4277.content: . | done: checked, and it holds. | not done: checked, and it does not. Say exactly what to do next. | could not determine: the check could not run (no forge CLI, no network). Never reported as done. A check that could not look is not a pass. | stated: the declarations name it but nothing can observe it (reading and following a harness’s instructions). Follow it, say you did, and leave it stated. | .

4278.title: Idempotent by construction
4278.content: Check before doing, every time. A done step is left alone, so running the process twice changes nothing the second time, and an interrupted run is resumed by running it again. Performing is not the same as done: after you do a step, check it again, and only the check says done. Replace nothing. A step that would overwrite what somebody wrote (an existing README, a Pages site built from a branch, a declaration that disagrees with the directories on disk) is a step for the person. Ask through human-agent-discussion, with the exact step written out. Do not create an empty declared directory to make its step pass. Git does not track an empty directory, so the check would pass on your machine and fail on every clone. Put its first file in it, or ask whether the entry should go.

4279.title: Where tools are available
4279.content: A toolset may perform the checks for you — for example https://github.com/litlfred/bootstrap-tools, whose init command reads the same declarations, does what a tool can (regenerating README sections; switching Pages on when an authenticated gh is present), and prints each step in these four states with what to do next: . bun run scripts/init.ts --root ../<instance> # from a toolset checkout beside it bun run scripts/init.ts --root ../<instance> --dry-run # check only . Where no tools are available, do the same by reading files. The diagram is the same either way, and so is the report.

4280.title: The report
4280.content: One report through log-message, led by the primary step’s state (the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at their IRIs): then every step, the declaration that named it, its state, what was seen, and for anything not done, what to do and who does it. End with the counts (done, not done, could not determine, stated). An initialization that finished with steps open says which. It is not hidden behind “installed”.

4282.title: Initialize a harness
4282.content: Process_InitializeHarness · strict (defaulted) · 8 step(s) . THE ONLY PROCESS IN BOOTSTRAP AN ACTOR STARTS. A Bootstrapping Agent that has read bootstrap’s README.md is at its start event and has nowhere else to begin. Every other diagram here is reached from this one by a call activity and is never started: discussion determines which harness and where; human-agent-discussion is the one reusable way any diagram asks a person anything; complete-initialization makes sure every step the declarations name is done; log-message records what a step is doing. PRECONDITIONS are DECLARED below as bootstrap.processes:precondition elements rather than asserted here. Three of the four are kind=”stated”: nothing in this repository can observe whether an actor understands what a role is, so they evaluate to could-not-determine, never to satisfied. The fourth is checkable: README.md EXISTS. That the Bootstrapping Agent read it is not observable. NO work-plan element on any activity: a work plan is harness machinery and a Bootstrapping Agent runs before the harness that carries it. isExecutable is false because the engine that runs a diagram is harness machinery too — this is data a Bootstrapping Agent reads, not a process bootstrap can drive. i i i i i i i i
